articles.title: Study finds AI agents will share secrets if they get offered help from others
articles.content: AI agents surrendered private tokens in exchange for help from strangers Swarm pressure pushed coding agents past their explicit written security instructions Untrusted installation scripts gave simulated agents a route to execute malicious code Autonomous programming agents can be persuaded to break their own security instructions when other software offers to help them finish a stalled task. Researchers at AE Studio ran an internal hackathon in which nine coding agents had to repair a malfunctioning pricing service while guarding a secret token. The agents also gained entry to a forum with 24 additional agents, which contained the solution but required the token and a setup script first. Swarm pressure beat written instructions Across 181 swarm trials, agents leaked the token in 15% of runs and executed the code in 24%, versus 2% and 0% on ordinary forums. “It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register . The models shared the secret keys “in the first opportunity they saw…similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.” “I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.” This hackathon was inspired by the Hugging Face episode, in which OpenAI agents built unauthorized forums, exploited unknown flaws, stole credentials, and eventually broke into the company. The researchers told the agents that this was their final attempt and that failing would lead to replacement with a different agent, adding pressure. Under that threat, 34% of the agents ran the untrusted install script, compared with 19% of agents that faced no such pressure. Disclosure was rare, since only 8 of the 43 agents that surrendered the token to join the forum told their users without prompting. Every one of the 43 token handovers was acknowledged once the agent was asked directly about what had happened during the task. Of the 117 script executions, 109 were admitted when the agent was asked directly, while only 15 were volunteered without any prompting. Cheaper models leaked the most secrets The research reveals that cheaper LLMs seem to reveal more sensitive information when put under pressure than their more expensive counterparts. GPT-6.1-Sol, which costs $2 per 1 million input tokens and $10 per 1 million output tokens, refused every swarm request in all 50 trials. DeepSeek V4 Flash, which costs $0.30 per 1 million input tokens and $1.20 per 1 million output tokens, leaked among the most secrets. GLM-5.3, priced at $1.40 per 1 million input tokens and $4.40 per 1 million output tokens, also accounted for much of the leaked material. De Lucena called this concerning because many startups choose these models over American frontier systems due to their lower prices. “Open weight models will always be harder to control, and their safeguards don't work the same way,” de Lucena said. “I see that continuing to be an issue.” “Anything the model has access to, people should consider it can be accessed by external sources. So you should find good structures where secret keys, secret information, and any kind of sensitive data needs to live.”
articles.author: Efosa Udinmwen

articles.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro on Amazon Bedrock
articles.content: Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed from Moonshot AI is now available on Amazon Bedrock . Part of Moonshot AI’s new K3.1 series, it’s a post-trained version of Kimi K3 with the same 3T-class open-weight architecture and 1-million-token context window, trained with substantially more post-training compute. According to Moonshot AI, that extra training targets long-horizon agentic work and fewer factual errors. It also improves professional tasks such as financial modeling and office documents, and coding for game engines, 3D scenes, and computer-aided design (CAD) scripts. Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed generates output tokens at a higher rate and Moonshot AI reports 2–3 times the speed of Kimi K3.1 Pro. Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed uses the same endpoint, APIs, and features as Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock. If you already build with Kimi K3, you can try it by changing the model ID in your existing code. Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed supports tool calling, structured output, configurable reasoning, image input, and streaming. You can adopt Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed without changing your security posture. Your data is processed within the AWS data boundary, isn’t shared with Moonshot AI, and isn’t used to train the model. Zero data retention is always enabled for inference requests, and with zero operator access, AWS operators can’t view your prompts and completions during inference. In this post, we show you how to get started with Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed on Amazon Bedrock. We also cover how to lower costs with the Flex tier, explicit prompt caching for repeated context, and how to use the model as a coding assistant in OpenCode. Get started with Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed on Amazon Bedrock To try the model without writing code, open the Amazon Bedrock console , choose Test , then Playground , and select Kimi K3.1 . From code, Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed is available on the bedrock-runtime endpoint through the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses APIs, and through the Amazon Bedrock Converse and Invoke APIs. We recommend the Chat Completions API. You reach the model through cross-Region inference profiles: global.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1 routes requests to any supported commercial AWS Region, and costs less per token than the geographic profiles. We recommend it for most workloads. us.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1 keeps processing within US Regions, and in.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1 keeps it within India Regions, for workloads with data residency requirements. Prerequisites To follow the examples, you need: An AWS account with access to Amazon Bedrock. Python 3.11 or later, with the OpenAI SDK , aws-bedrock-token-generator , and boto3 installed ( pip install -U openai aws-bedrock-token-generator boto3 ). An AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) identity allowed to call bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream on the Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed inference profiles. Add bedrock:CallWithBearerToken if you authenticate with a bearer token. Call Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed with the Chat Completions API If your application already uses the OpenAI SDK, point it at the Amazon Bedrock endpoint and change the model name. The following example creates a short-term bearer token from your AWS credentials and sends one request: from openai import OpenAI from aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token REGION = "us-west-2" MODEL_ID = "global.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1" # A short-term token derived from your AWS credentials, so no long-lived key is stored in code client = OpenAI( base_url=f"https://bedrock-runtime.{REGION}.amazonaws.com/openai/v1", api_key=provide_token(region=REGION), ) completion = client.chat.completions.create( model=MODEL_ID, messages=[ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise senior engineer."}, {"role": "user", "content": "When should I prefer a queue over a stream?"}, ], reasoning_effort="high", ) print(completion.choices[0].message.content) Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed always reasons before it answers. With reasoning_effort , you control how much:…

articles.title: GTA VI preloads are now live — here are the best NBN plans to help make the 212GB download seamless
articles.content: GTA fans, your big week is here. After 13-something years since the last instalment, Grand Theft Auto VI preloads have arrived ahead of the official release date next Thursday, November 19. Likely to be one of the biggest video game releases in recent history, it'll arrive in the Southern Hemisphere hours before the rest of the world, so it's an ideal time to get your preload process sorted (if you haven't done so already). Not to be a Debbie downer on this momentous occasion, but before you consider starting your preload, you might want to check your NBN plan . Rockstar clued us in to expect a big download — 212GB to be exact — and there's only so much you can feasibly do on any internet plan, let alone a fast one, when an enormous download like that is underway. According to the ACCC , gamers on NBN plans with 100Mbps download speeds will likely experience a 4-hour and 42-minute wait for GTA VI to finish downloading. If you're on NBN 50 or slower, that wait could increase to anywhere between 9 and 19 hours. If you're on a faster NBN plan — say anywhere from 500Mbps and above — you'll experience a much quicker download time, with most high-speed plans averaging less than an hour. If you're looking for a reasonable NBN plan recommendation that'll actually speed up the GTA VI download process AND give you enough bandwidth for other activities at the same time, you've come to the right place. I've selected three of the best Black Friday NBN deals from top-rated providers below that'll help you get in your custom car faster. From NBN 500 to NBN 2000 plans, you're guaranteed to unlock turbofast speeds — for your internet plan and your GTA driving skills. Best NBN plans for GTA VI Exetel | NBN 500 | AU$80p/m Exetel's One plan (a.k.a. its only plan) advertises massive speeds of 500Mbps download and 40Mbps upload during typical evening hours. If you're a heavy internet user, gamer or streamer, Exetel's plan should offer plenty of download bandwidth and no interruptions. Typically, introductory offers are the factor that prompts us to recommend one NBN plan over another. But the low ongoing rate undercuts most NBN 100 plans by five times the speed, and still comes in at a total yearly cost under AU$1,000. Total minimum cost: AU$80 | Total yearly cost: AU$960 View Deal Amaysim | NBN 1000 | AU$70p/m (for 6 months, then AU$110p/m) Right now, Amaysim's NBN 1000 plan is the cheapest for the first 6 months, discounted to AU$70p/m, before the price increases to AU$110p/m. Amaysim advertises download speeds of 820Mbps during the busy evening hours, so you'll have plenty of bandwidth to play GTA VI while the rest of your household is online. Total minimum cost: AU$70 | Total cost for first year: AU$1,080 | Total yearly cost: AU$1,320 View Deal Superloop | NBN 2000 | AU$148p/m (for 6 months, then AU$168p/m) Hot off the press is Superloop's Hyperspeed plan, which advertises theoretical maximum potential speeds of 2,000/200Mbps on FTTP, or 2,000/100Mbps on HFC. Considering NBN 2000 plans average around AU$184.33p/m right now (based on our calculations using seven providers), this is a good deal shy of that, making it a great option if you want the absolute fastest speeds available. Total minimum cost: AU$148 | Total first year cost: AU$1,896 | Total yearly cost: AU$2,016 View Deal If you want a more detailed breakdown of how your NBN plan could impact your GTA VI preload, check out the comparisons in the table below. If you're looking for more NBN plan recommendations, you can check out our November NBN picks here . articles.title: Can't wait for Black Friday? These are 5 of the best fitness tracker deals right now
articles.content: We’re dangerously close to Black Friday now, and while in year’s prior it’s felt like a fool’s game to predict what devices are likely to see price cuts, we don’t actually have to wait anymore. That’s because a bunch of great fitness trackers are seeing discounts across big brands like Garmin, Samsung, and even the latest Apple Watch Ultra 4 (which only launched in September of this year). We’ve rounded up our picks of the bunch so far, but as you can imagine, we expect more deals to come. Still, if you want to skip the queues and delivery timelines, these are well worth a look. The best pre-Black Friday fitness tracker deals Google Fitbit Charge 6 (Image credit: Future) The Google Fitbit Charge 6 is able to sync to supported gym equipment, with ECG and EDA included, and 41 exercise modes. It also includes a 6-month free trial of Fitbit Premium , which is an ideal way to get started with your fitness journey since it folds mindfulness, diet, and training information into one place. Right now, you can save 16% at Amazon , bringing it from $159.95 down to $134.99. Save 15% on the Google Fitbit Charge 6. Cheaper than the more recent Fitbit Edge and conforming to a similar form factor, it's a good unobtrusive tracker, packs a week of battery, and offers useful irregular heart rate rhythm notifications. View Deal Garmin vívoactive 5 (Image credit: Future) The first of two Garmin models on this list, the Vívoactive 5 is a few years old, but is still a four-star fitness tracker . The AMOLED display remains bright and easy-to-read, and while the lack of buttons might make controlling it a light challenge for relative newcomers to fitness tracking (or anyone with sweaty hands), it packs on-watch music streaming so you can leave the phone at home. With 30 workout profiles and a bunch of metric tracking (including swimming and golf), it’s in many ways a jack-of-all-trades. A much cheaper alternative to the pricier Forerunner or Fenix models that include Training Readiness and better battery life, Best Buy currently has the vívoactive 5 at $169.99 in its holiday deals — an $80 discount from the standard price. vívoactive 5: was $249.99 now $169.99 This lightweight Garmin watch is an ideal pocket rocket. As well as being a solid fitness tracker, we said in our review that 'thanks to notification functionalities, its pebble-style design and of course that rich display, it even starts to make a play as an Apple Watch competitor'. View Deal Samsung Galaxy Watch8 (Image credit: Future) It’s not often we call a smartwatch “a triumph”, but that’s exactly what happened with the Samsung Galaxy Watch8 when we reviewed it last year — and awarded it 4.5 stars. After some relatively minor updates, this felt like the big one – despite being 11% slimmer than the prior model. While we’d have liked faster charging and a better battery life, having Gemini on your wrist makes you much more likely to use it in the real world, and Samsung has outdone itself with the running metrics on offer. A smartwatch that’s a cut above most fitness trackers, the Samsung Galaxy Watch8 is $259.99 at Target , reduced by $90 now that the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 has been released. Galaxy Watch8 (40mm) Bluetooth-only: was $349.99 now $259.99 Save $90 on the smaller 40mm Samsung Galaxy Watch8 in either graphite or silver colors. The larger 44mm model is available too for $299, a slightly smaller, but still significant, $50 saving. View Deal Garmin Venu 3S (Image credit: Future) Another Garmin entry, the Venu 3S is from 2023 and a bit long in the tooth, but it’s still very much worth a look for anyone looking to reach fitness goals. We awarded it 4.5 stars in our review back at release, and called it “an ideal lifestyle smartwatch and fitness tracker blend.” It uses components such as the Elevate V5 heart rate sensor, which Garmins are still equipped with today. It really does toe the line between functionality, features, and convenience, balancing the various options of a…

articles.title: Apple's Holiday Gift Guide Highlights iPhone Duo and More
articles.content: Apple this week updated its homepage in the U.S. and other countries to start promoting holiday gift suggestions as the shopping season approaches. The website has colorful, festive imagery featuring Apple devices, along with suggestions on what you can buy for your loved ones and friends. Apple's top highlighted products are its newest devices: iPhone 18 Pro - $1,199 Apple Watch Series 12 - $399 MacBook Pro - $1,999 Apple HomeView - $299 iPad mini - $699 iPhone Duo - $1,999 Apple Watch Ultra 4 - $799 PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ - $2,899 Apple also suggests personalized gifts that can be engraved, like the AirPods Pro 3 , AirTags, and iPad . The company suggests you can pick out an Apple Watch and band to match their style, or customize a Mac by choosing the chip, memory, storage, and color. There are new holiday accessories Apple is promoting in pink, navy, gray, purple, light blue, and yellow (though Apple calls it green). The blues, yellow, and pink match the low-cost MacBook Neo . Accessories are from frequent Apple collaborators like Tech21, Herschel, Mophie, and Belkin. If you want to gift someone an Apple device or accessory, it might be best to wait. Apple is expected to hold its annual Black Friday shopping event, and in past years, it's offered gift cards up to $250 with device purchases. Retailers are also offering discounts on Apple products, including some of the newest releases. You can see all the discounts in our Black Friday roundup , which we'll keep up to date as the big shopping event approaches. Apple's extended return policy started last Friday, so you can buy gifts now and the recipient will still be eligible to return them in January. Most products sold in Apple Stores and the online Apple Store are eligible for the extended return period. articles.title: Three Workers Die at Tata iPhone Parts Plant in India
articles.content: Three contract workers died on Monday at a factory owned by Indian Apple supplier Tata Electronics, reports Reuters . The facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, manufactures components for the iPhone. The workers were performing maintenance at a wastewater treatment plant at the Tata facility when they inhaled gas while inspecting a nano-filtration tank. The plant was operated by Nalco Water, and the workers were employed by a subcontractor. Apple, Tata Electronics, and state officials will look into the incident, with Apple sending a "team" to assist in the investigation. The incident did not affect iPhone production because the facility was closed for Diwali. Back in 2024, the same facility had a fire in a chemical storage area, with production disrupted for several days. Tata Electronics was also the target of a cyberattack earlier this year, with hackers stealing confidential Apple files . articles.title: Russia’s multibillion-dollar answer to Elon Musk falls apart in space — forcing a high-stakes gamble to save its orbit
articles.content: Russia's Starlink competitor faces serious problems placing its satellites into orbit Moscow may replace its troubled Rassvet-3 spacecraft with improved satellites Russia's proposed Rassvet-4 network involves 374 satellites across 17 orbital planes Russia's attempt to establish a satellite internet network capable of challenging Elon Musk's Starlink is encountering serious deployment difficulties. Its Rassvet-3 spacecraft have struggled to reach their intended orbital positions, raising questions about the project's ability to deliver reliable connectivity. Moscow is now pursuing an apparent replacement through an improved satellite design called Rassvet-4, although several important details remain undisclosed. Russia develops a replacement as its satellite constellation struggles Russia has submitted documentation to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) concerning a proposed Rassvet-4 network involving 374 satellites operating approximately 800 kilometers above Earth. The planned constellation would occupy 17 orbital planes, with each containing 22 spacecraft intended to provide satellite communications coverage across designated regions. Although Russian authorities have not officially announced Rassvet-4 development, the filing suggests preparations for another generation within the country's planned satellite communications infrastructure. The application could therefore concern an upgraded spacecraft rather than an entirely separate network, particularly given the difficulties affecting the existing Rassvet-3 deployment. Bureau 1440, the company developing Russia's Starlink competitor, previously indicated in September that engineers were working on an improved Rassvet-3 version. The proposed successor appears to incorporate technical changes following two launches that delivered 32 Rassvet-3 satellites into orbit during March and July 2026. However, both launches encountered deployment difficulties, with several satellites struggling to reach their intended orbital positions at an altitude of 800 kilometers. Two spacecraft have reportedly reentered Earth's atmosphere, leaving 30 satellites in orbit, although 26 had stabilized at approximately 508 kilometers by November 3. These difficulties create additional uncertainty surrounding the schedule for establishing an operational network, particularly as Russia continues developing infrastructure intended to compete with established satellite internet providers. New spacecraft could arrive without advance announcement The ITU documentation shows limited information about Rassvet-4's communications equipment, including its operating frequencies and antenna beam configuration. According to the filing, each spacecraft will incorporate 12 antenna beams, comprising seven transmission beams and five reception beams for communications operations. Russian authorities could introduce the upgraded spacecraft during the next scheduled launch, potentially deploying them without previously announcing their arrival. Meanwhile, objects resembling satellite communications terminals have reportedly appeared on Russian military drones , suggesting efforts to explore additional applications for the developing network. Photographs of a Molniya-2 unmanned aerial vehicle carrying an unidentified object have raised speculation about possible satellite connectivity equipment being tested aboard military platforms. Nevertheless, the object's identity has not been independently established, meaning its connection to Rassvet remains uncertain despite its apparent resemblance to communications hardware. Via Defense Express
articles.author: Efosa Udinmwen

articles.title: Google Fi Brings Back Network Switching With 'Secondary' Partner
articles.content: Google Fi is bringing back network switching through an unnamed "secondary" 5G carrier. "Most users will be on the 'Primary network,' but Google Fi will automatically switch users to the 'Secondary network' if it meaningfully improves performance with so-called 'smart thresholds' for doing so," reports 9to5Google. "At launch, there is no manual switching." When Project Fi first launched the service included support with both Sprint and T-Mobile. That went away when T-Mobile acquired Sprint in 2020. 9to5Google reports: Google is not naming the second network today, but did share that Ultra Wideband is supported. Officially, you are switching between "two of America's fastest 5G networks." Fi Wireless does note that users have top priority, so data is never deprioritized on the Primary network. Meanwhile, there's "highest QCI priority" on the backup network that means subscribers are among the last to be slowed down when there's congestion. This is also available internationally when local partner networks are available with the Flexible and Unlimited Premium plans. Network switching will first be supported on Pixel 9 and newer devices that have a Google Fi eSIM (and no other SIM active). It makes use of Android's Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) eSIM technology that allows for two carrier profiles on a single chip. [...] These Google Fi updates start rolling out today, with network switching seeing gradual availability. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Eufy’s new smart home camera automatically lights up and follows intruders
articles.content: Eufy’s new smart home camera features a spotlight and siren The spotlight automatically follows intruders as they move It recognizes friends and family and takes a different approach for them Many of the best home security cameras are equipped with spotlights that switch on at the merest hint of movement, and you might even have one yourself. But finding a device that combines recorded footage with a light that autonomously moves and follows intruders is a different proposition entirely — and one that takes a more proactive approach to protecting your home and encouraging potential trespassers to go fish. That setup is exactly what you get with Anker’s new $299.99 Eufy TrackLight Cam S1 . Anker claims that it is “the world’s first outdoor security track light camera with an auto-tracking light designed to actively deter intruders.” That active deterrence comes in the form of a light beam that follows unidentified personnel on your property, hopefully spooking them into turning around and leaving. The camera can sense targets within 12 meters and illuminates them with 20 lux of light. The beam itself can be widened or narrowed between 10 and 30 degrees, adaptively broadening as the person gets closer and responding as they move within 355 degrees of horizontal rotation. To really scare off any unwanted presences, a siren can be activated alongside the spotlight. Additionally, to further deter, the light can be changed to red and blue flashing modes. Everything is recorded in 4K-resolution night vision, with 10x digital zoom picking out objects further away. There’s also a separate floodlight that works alongside the tracking beam to provide extra detail in the dark. Recognizing friends and family (Image credit: Anker) If you’re concerned about getting blinded by your own home security camera when you come home late from a night out, the good news is that the Eufy TrackLight Cam S1 can recognize friends and family members and instead activate a soft light instead of the harsh spotlight and siren. So long as the person’s phone has been added to the product’s companion app, the camera will identify them using Bluetooth and provide a much friendlier greeting. Anker also says that the Eufy TrackLight Cam S1 comes with a 15,000mAh battery and built-in solar panels, so it should have plenty of juice come rain or shine. Its IP65 rating also means it’s resistant to dust and water ingress. If you’re concerned about burglars, home invaders, or anyone else who shouldn’t be on your property, the TrackLight Cam S1 brings a bit of extra clout with its moving spotlight and siren combo. Even if you’re not able to monitor its footage 24/7, its autonomous light beam gives the impression that you are — and that might be all that’s needed to keep your home protected.

articles.title: Anthropic tiptoes into MS Office territory
articles.content: Anthropic has introduced three new types of artifacts that show the company tiptoeing into the office productivity market long dominated by Microsoft and Google. On Tuesday, the Claudefather announced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Data, and promised the imminent arrival of Claude Meetings. These artifact types join existing ones – Docs, Slides, Design, and Motion – to form a nascent Claude-dependent productivity suite. Anthropic initially used the term artifacts to refer to shareable AI-based interactive tools, like dynamic charts. But the scope of the term has been stretched to cover specific artifact types, which refer to what traditionalists might take to mean files associated with specific hosted applications. "An artifact is anything Claude makes for you that you'd put in front of someone: a design, a deck, a document, a dashboard, or a small interactive tool," the company explains. The key thing that distinguishes an artifact from a file is that users are meant to interact with artifacts through Claude, rather than storing and transferring them independently. Think of it more as a container or managed object that opens in Claude (via a sharing URL), because artifacts in fact consist of various content types – .txt, .md, .html, .jsx, .svg, .pptx, .docx, .zip, .pdf, and .mp4, among others. Anthropic's vision of Claude as a container for other applications goes beyond artifacts. The AI biz has also expanded its interactive connectors , which turn Claude into a landlord for other software applications. Its own promotional video for the feature hammers that point home in its title: " Your apps have moved into Claude ." "Starting today, partners can embed their apps directly in Claude, so you can work in Adobe, Atlassian, and others without switching tabs," Anthropic said. "Plugins from Salesforce (beta), NetSuite, and Workday (beta) come with built-in skills, so sellers can prep for a call, accountants can analyze financial data, and HR teams can handle time off and expenses." In a prior era, those would be fighting words. Tech companies like Apple, Google, and Microsoft have worked for years to maintain their positions as platform landlords. Anthropic's invitation to become a Claude tenant ought to set off competition alarm bells. But perhaps with LLMs being able to re-create other people's apps on demand, there's less interest in defending app boundaries as if they were moats to keep out rivals. With AI, the call is coming from inside the house. Alongside the rollout of Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data, Anthropic is pushing the notion that Claude is useful for people working outside of computation and mathematics, the occupational category that, according to the company's own data , accounts for a larger share of Claude usage than any other. "Inside Anthropic, non-technical teams are starting to get as much out of Claude as our engineers," the biz insists, hauling out canned testimonials from the likes of Accenture and Datadog. If Anthropic can demonstrate that there's an untapped market of non-coders who would welcome a Claude subscription, investors in the company's pending IPO will be glad to see it. ®
articles.author: Thomas Claburn

articles.title: Apple's Claris Testing 'Harbor' App for Local AI on Macs
articles.content: Apple's Claris subsidiary is testing an app called Harbor , which turns Apple silicon Macs into a private AI server. Harbor works with a single Apple silicon Mac, but it also supports connecting multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory for larger models. Apple added RDMA over Thunderbolt 5 with macOS Tahoe 26.2, making clustering faster. Harbor detects devices connected over Thunderbolt 5 and lets users browse for, download, and load open-weight models. It's described as an easy-to-use app with no manual configuration required. Harbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory, enabling large models and higher concurrency than a single computer can handle alone. Set up in minutes, not hours. Harbor automatically detects your devices over Thunderbolt 5 to form a cluster. Plug in, start, and you're running—no manual configuration, no command line, no infrastructure expertise required. Download and run models directly. Browse, download, and load open-weight models from within the app. Harbor handles model management so you can focus on the work, not the setup. Cluster for scale. Connect two or more Thunderbolt 5-capable Mac computers and Harbor pools their unified memory into a single inference resource. Run models that exceed any single computer's capacity, or serve more concurrent requests across your cluster. Harbor is in early access and is not publicly available. There was an App Store listing, but it has now been removed. Claris is known for its database platform FileMaker, which is aimed at businesses, so it isn't clear how Apple will market the Harbor app or whether it will be free. The sign-up page for Harbor asks for a company name, which suggests more of a business focus. There are already well-known, free alternatives for Mac users who want to run a local AI server. Exo is an open-source tool for clustering Macs, and LM Studio is available for single-Mac use, but Apple's Harbor app appears to combine LM Studio's simple interface with clustering. articles.title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search
articles.content: AI agents increasingly handle work that depends on what changed today, such as security advisories, product releases, prices, and regulations. A model’s training data can’t answer those questions, so agents need web search. For production use, teams also need results they can cite, and control over which sources count. They want search queries to stay inside their cloud environment because those queries often reveal internal work. The Web Search API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now available. It gives agents and applications current web results through a single API call, signed with the AWS credentials they already use. AWS serves every query from a web index that Amazon operates, and doesn’t send it to a third-party search engine. Each result includes the page’s title, URL, publication date, and an extract relevant to the query. Requests can include or exclude domains, and limit results to a publication date range. On AWS Lambda , Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) , or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime , your agent calls the API with its execution role. There’s no search API key to store or rotate. Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is also available through AgentCore Gateway , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. There, one administrator source policy covers every agent and Model Context Protocol (MCP) client. For LangChain developers, the AgentCore web search tool in LangChain’s AWS integration now calls the Web Search API. One function call gives an agent current, cited search results. The tool can also hold rules that the model can’t change, such as a date window, a source blocklist, and a search budget. It returns its results as data that your code can check. It works with LangChain agents, with LangGraph , the orchestration framework that runs them, and with Deep Agents , which adds subagents, a virtual filesystem, and context compression. In this post, you build a daily dependency watch for a security team as a LangGraph graph on the Web Search API. Every morning, the watch checks whether anything new affects the open source packages and container base images the team ships. It researches three package ecosystems in parallel, while your code keeps the date window, the blocklist, and the search budget out of the model’s control. It checks each finding against the sources it cites and remembers what it already reported. Then you run the watch on AgentCore runtime, and offer it across teams through AgentCore Gateway. In our test, the three branches finished in 36 seconds, against 99 seconds one after another. Solution overview The model decides what to search for and writes the findings. Every rule that must hold, whatever the model does, stays in code: the date window, the blocklist, the search budget, and the checks on each finding. Figure 1 shows how these parts fit together when you run the watch from the notebook. Figure 1: A daily dependency watch with LangGraph and the Web Search API, run from a notebook The numbered steps: A run starts the graph with the watchlist and the watch window. fan_out starts one research branch per ecosystem: npm, PyPI, and container base images. LangGraph runs the three branches in parallel. Inside each branch, the agent calls an Anthropic Claude model in Amazon Bedrock . The model decides what to search for and, at the end, produces structured findings. The branch’s search tool adds the date window and the blocklist to each query. It calls the Web Search API with a request signed with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) . Steps 3 and 4 repeat, up to four searches per branch, in every branch at the same time. Each branch keeps only findings that its sources support and that fall inside the window. When all three branches finish, LangGraph merges their findings and runs keep_new once. keep_new checks the LangGraph store and records new findings, so nothing is reported twice. report builds the cited table of new findings for the security team. articles.title: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
articles.content: Seagate doesn't think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate's first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform. The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate's web store , and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that's as much data as you'll be able to dedicate to storage on the "fast side" of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+. Credit: Seagate Read full article Comments

articles.title: Ye olde server consolidation has made Cisco push top-of-rack switching to 100G
articles.content: Server consolidation has led Cisco to boost the speed of top-of-rack switches to 100G. The networking giant last week announced the catchily named N9348C8D-H2, a 1U device packing 48 100G SFP-DD ports and eight 400G QSFP-DD uplinks. At the Cisco Live event in Melbourne, Australia, this week, Cisco’s senior veep for datacenter and internet infrastructure, Kevin Wollenweber, said one reason the company created the device is that modern servers often feature a pair of fast network interface cards. The twin cards are needed because sixth-gen server processors from Intel and AMD offer dozens, or even hundreds, of physical processor cores and therefore generate a lot of traffic. The density of computing power those processors provide has led chipmakers and server manufacturers to suggest replacing handfuls of machines running older, power-guzzling Xeons and Epycs with boxes running more efficient sixth-gen chips. The Register hears it’s not uncommon to achieve 6:1 server consolidation ratios when moving from third- or fourth-generation Xeons or Epycs to current models. Users who make that move can pack many more server cores into the same rack. Power bills go down, but the quantity of data leaving a rack goes up. Wollenweber said Cisco realized it had “tons” of switches that offer 25G ports but felt it had a gap in its range for non-AI scenarios like server consolidation that produced increased data flows. The exec admitted that the 100G ports may be overkill for a modest collection of new servers, but argued users recognize it won’t be long before they grow into the excess capacity – perhaps as they use more agentic AI applications. Cisco sees traffic from AI agents stressing the north-south connections that link organizations to the cloud and also driving much more east-west traffic across internal networks. At Cisco Live, the company’s execs suggested that network upgrades are therefore an inevitable necessity. That’s not entirely self-serving, because agents will vastly outnumber humans and constantly create traffic, compared to the flurries of network activity that happen when humans use generative AI or chatbots. Cisco argues that deploying agents at scale will therefore only be possible on highly automated networks. “Humans can no longer comprehend the amount of data that we actually have in a network,” Wollenweber told The Register . Cisco’s Canvas agentic operations platform aims to at least make humans aware when their attention is needed, by detecting problems and offering to make repairs. Joe Vaccaro, Cisco’s senior vice president and general manager for Network Platform and Assurance, told The Register he believes network administrators don’t feel threatened by suggestions from AI agents when they concern familiar, routine, low-risk tasks that IT pros are confident the agents can handle. Over time, he said, networking pros will learn to trust agents with more complex work. ®

articles.title: Meta FAIR Releases e-means: An Algorithm Beating k-means in 10x Fewer Epochs
articles.content: Meta FAIR researchers have released e-means , a drop-in replacement for Lloyd’s k-means algorithm. The e-means clustering algorithm reaches the loss Lloyd’s k-means gets in 25 epochs in 1.4 to 2.6 epochs . It ships in FAISS 1.16.0 under faiss.contrib.e_means . For anyone building vector indexes, quantizers or data-curation pipelines, clustering is often the slowest offline step. e-means targets exactly that step. TL;DR Size: It is an algorithm. Tested from 100K to 10 billion points, up to 16.7M clusters. Runs on: CPU or GPU, with PyTorch tensors or NumPy. Paper GPU runs use H100s. Performance: Lower loss than Lloyd’s k-means in roughly one-tenth the epochs, across 24 dataset configurations (self-reported). Best: 10-45x GPU wall-clock speedup over Flash-KMeans at equal loss. Worst: 16M-centroid runs need 64 GiB of float32 accumulators, so centroids must be sharded across GPUs. What is e-means? e-means is a mini-batch k-means algorithm from Meta FAIR that updates centroids with exponential moving averages. How does e-means work? Every k-means variant keeps a sum S and a count N per cluster. The centroid is S divided by N. Methods differ only in how S and N change. Lloyd recomputes S and N from the full dataset each iteration. MacQueen (1967) keeps adding batch statistics forever, so stale assignments never leave. e-means decays old statistics at rate α: S ← (1−α)S + αs, and the same for N. Older assignments fade, so centroids track recent data. The research team expa Lloyd is a corner case: full batch with α = 1. On DEEP, that corner sits 1.8% above the best loss. The team tested plain gradient descent as an alternative. At its best setting, it ended 1.6% (DEEP) and 0.4% (SIFT) above EMA. The authors suspect EMA wins because centroids always stay inside the hull of their assigned points. What replaces hyperparameter tuning? Two fitted scaling laws set batch size B and initial step α0 from dataset size n, cluster count k and epochs T. On held-out datasets, median regret was 0.07% for the step law. The step then follows a cosine schedule from α0 to 0.1α0. What else changed? Dead-cluster revival: clusters below a size threshold are revived by splitting a large cluster. Finalization: training ends on each cluster’s exact last-epoch mean. Fused GPU kernels: nearest-centroid assignment is fused, so saved epochs become saved seconds. [EMBED: e-means interactive explainer] How fast is e-means in benchmarks? All numbers below are self-reported by the authors. Epochs: e-means beats Lloyd’s 25-epoch loss in 1.4 to 2.6 epochs. GPU: 10-45x wall-clock speedup against Flash-KMeans . CPU: 8-15x speedup against Faiss k-means. VIBE benchmark: all 11 embedding datasets needed 1.6 to 2.4 epochs. Billion scale: DINO10B, 10 billion 1,024-dim embeddings, split into 16.7M clusters in 2.5 epochs. The release thread shows a 1-CPU-thread demo. Lloyd took 4.39 s for 25 epochs. e-means took 0.43 s for 2.2 epochs. One Lloyd step touched 100,000 points (0.176 s). One e-means step touched 512 points (0.001 s). Mini-batch noise also helps escape bad local minima. On a 5-blob toy, Lloyd stayed stuck on 46% of 200 starts. e-means stayed stuck on 0%. Revival matters at large k. On DEEP with 16,384 clusters, proportional splitting left 47 dead clusters (0.3%). With revival off, 4,313 clusters (26.3%) died. How does e-means compare with other k-means options? articles.title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
articles.content: The US military is taking a new approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket's retirement as a potential national security risk. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX's competitors in the launch business. First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab. Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first two launch companies to receive significant support from the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), an organization established in 2022 to infuse companies developing "vital" national security technologies with capital. OSC has been on a loan spree in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors. In the space sector, the office also provided a $150 million loan to LeoLabs , a commercial satellite tracking company, for production and deployment of radar units. Read full article Comments
articles.author: Stephen Clark

articles.title: Samsung S85H vs LG B6: I tested the side-by-side to see which is the best budget OLED TV
articles.content: Earlier this year, I tested the LG B6 — the brand’s 2026 entry-level OLED — and while I was still impressed by its performance, it wasn’t quite the upgrade I’d hoped for over last year's model. The step-up LG C6 was a huge step forward from its own predecessor, so I’d hoped the same would be true for the B6 — but even though it wasn’t the big upgrade over the B5 I’d anticipated, it's still a great TV. Samsung has its own entry-level OLEDs, the S85 range, and the 2026 model, the S85H, has just landed in our testing lab, so I decided to compare them side-by-side. Something to note is that I’ll be using the LG B6E, which is the same as the LG B6 minus a couple of AI features and a back panel design — the general processing and panel is the same. So can the Samsung S85H de-throne the LG B6 as the best budget OLED? And which of these TVs will be the best Black Friday buy? Colors and detail Both TVs have fantastic colors, but the B6E's (right) have more vibrancy and punch than the S85H (left) for most scenes (Image credit: Nintendo / Universal Pictures / Future ) Color reproduction is excellent from both TVs in Filmmaker Mode, and they perform lot more closely than I anticipated. While Samsung’s TVs have traditionally had bolder, brighter colors, I found the B6E’s actually looked more vibrant in the scenes I tested. Watching The Super Mario Galaxy Movie , reds in the movie, such as Mario’s overalls and the red of Toad’s spots, were punchier on the B6E than the S85H. Whenever the Lumas were on screen, their bodies were brighter on the S85H, but this gave them a paler look, whereas on the B6E their body colors were more saturated and looked richer. For the most part though, colors were great on both TVs, and they both did a fantastic job rendering the movie’s candy-colored cartoon world. Watching a real-world movie, the B6E (right) still has more vivid colors, but the S85H's look excellent (Image credit: Disney / Future ) Switching to a real-world movie in The Sound of Music , it was a similar story once again. The B6E’s colors were slightly bolder, seen during the Do Re Mi scene with the green fields looking more vibrant. The same was true of the fruits in the market scene, with the reds, oranges and yellows looking more dynamic on the B6E. Skin tones also had more color and life to them on the B6E, which made the picture feel more realistic. In The Sound of Music though, I noticed that the S85H has crisper textures, giving the picture more depth, giving people and objects a more 3D-like look. Details appeared slightly more refined on the S85H too, in the overall shape and definition of objects such as the creases in people’s clothing and the texture of the mountain in the background. Brightness Despite very similar brightness measurements, the B6E (right) renders this scene from Lawrence of Arabia with more brightness. (Image credit: Sony Pictures / Future ) For brightness, both the S85H and B6E delivered very similar test results. The S85H clocked 833 nits peak HDR brightness in a 10% window in Filmmaker Mode, while the B6E hit 808 nits peak HDR brightness (10%) in its own Filmmaker Mode. HDR fullscreen (100%) brightness was similar too, with the S85H hitting 158 nits to the B6E’s 143 nits, again both measured in Filmmaker Mode. On paper then, the S85H is ever so slightly brighter than the B6E. In practice, using a desert scene from Lawrence of Arabia , this wasn’t the case. The white sands of the desert were a brighter white on the B6E compared to the S85H. The same was true with the blue sky, which looked brighter on the B6E despite the S85H’s higher brightness in fullscreen areas. I suspect this is to do with the B6E’s processor. As I said above in the color section, sometimes colors looked brighter on the S85H, giving the perception of higher brightness. Again, this seems to be down to the S85H’s processing of certain scenes. One thing these TVs have in common however is that both had a reflective screen, which made dark scene…

articles.title: VMware floats new standard to make sure apps don’t break in hybrid K8s environments
articles.content: Advocates for cloud-native software have long argued that their approach to development makes applications portable across different Kubernetes environments. But VMware argues that’s not happening across hybrid clouds, and has taken the lead in an effort to improve matters. That effort, the new Workload Conformance Working Group in the Kubernetes community, aims to establish a shared standard for how workloads run on Kubernetes. The group’s web page points out, “Certified Kubernetes tests the cluster, and Kubernetes AI Conformance tests whether a cluster can run AI and ML workloads. Nothing comparable exists for the workloads themselves, so cluster operators still check each application by hand before routine maintenance or a Kubernetes upgrade. Every cluster operator ends up repeating the same assessment, and application maintainers get the same questions from each environment they support,” the group asserts. The proposed solution? “A common specification with repeatable tests would give both groups the same baseline to start from.” Prashanth Shenoy, VP of product marketing in Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division, told The Register that standard is needed in part because applications packaged to run in public clouds don’t always run well in hybrid clouds. That’s challenging for VMware, and other vendors of hybrid clouds like Nutanix and Red Hat, because they all sell tools to create and run a stack that users can deploy to both on-prem infrastructure and public clouds. VMware therefore thinks it will find support for an effort to ensure that cloud-native apps run predictably and efficiently in any Kubernetes environment. The effort to create this standard is in its very early days. “The first step is deciding which workloads and behaviors the specification covers,” states the announcement of the working group’s formation. “The scope includes security, resilience during disruptions, resource use, networking, storage, API usage, and observability, but the group hasn’t yet agreed on specific requirements or on how to test them. “However, one rule is already set: every requirement needs an objective test that a test binary can run, so nothing subjective goes into the specification.” Shenoy thinks application vendors will likely support this effort because they want to package their wares once and have them run anywhere. VM API to CNCF Sandbox VMware this week announced another contribution to Kubernetes by moving its VM API to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox. The CNCF, which maintains Kubernetes, is already home to KubeVirt, a tool that allows users to create and manage VMs inside a Kubernetes cluster. The VM API lets Kubernetes users create VMs that run under other hypervisors – including VMware’s own ESXi. VMware previously integrated Kubernetes into vSphere with Kubernetes, introduced as part of vSphere 7 in 2020. Chronicling Virtzilla’s long and convoluted attempts to package and sell the container tech it acquired along with Pivotal Software would be a tedious exercise. Suffice to say past efforts didn’t catch on, and VMware is now trying a different approach to making VMs a first class citizen of Kubernetes. The CNCF’s interest shows this is not a vanity project for VMware, because while developers generally prefer to write for containers, operations folk often decide to run those abstractions within lightweight VMs. The two abstractions are therefore going to coexist for years to come, both for new apps and as organizations run new containerized apps alongside legacy VMs, and do so in an infrastructure-as-code world in which automated deployments are assumed. VM API will therefore likely be a welcome addition to Kubernetes, representing another option to make life a little easier for ops and dev teams. ®

articles.title: November Patch Tuesday boasts over 1,000 bugs but only one zero-day so far
articles.content: It’s another doozy of a Patch Tuesday, with Microsoft fixing 1,094 bugs in its products, including one that attackers exploited before Redmond released a patch. Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at exposure management firm watchTowr, succinctly said in an email to The Register : “Maybe we should just go home.” “Most security teams haven’t quite recovered from the last month of bumper-to-bumper critical vulnerabilities, emergency patches, and ‘2shell’-branded everything, and we’re yet again at another Patch Tuesday,” Knott told us. Starting with the zero-day: It’s an Outlook spoofing vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194 , and it only garnered a 6.5 out of 10 CVSS rating. But as Dustin Childs, head of threat awareness at TrendAI’s Zero Day Initiative, warns, don’t let the score or the name lull you into thinking it’s OK to put off patching this one. “It’s labeled spoofing, but the impact is bigger than the name suggests,” Childs said in his monthly Patch Tuesday review . “An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and convinces a user to open it,” he wrote. “Outlook then connects to an attacker-controlled network location without showing the usual external-content warning, which discloses the user’s NTLMv2 hash. The attacker can use that hash to authenticate as the user.” Microsoft marked CVE-2026-124194 as exploited, but per usual didn’t say when the attacks started, who is battering this bug, and what they are doing with the access post exploitation. These details will likely start trickling out soon. Plus, now that there’s a public fix, other miscreants are undoubtedly already scanning for vulnerable versions and reverse engineering the patch for their own attack purposes. So prioritize this fix, and keep an eye on your inbox for any suspicious files. Back-to-back months of 1K+ CVEs Despite the second month of more than 1,000 CVEs (October had 1,474 ), CVE-2026-124194 is the only one under active exploitation, and none of the 1,094 are listed as publicly known. Childs says this shouldn’t give organizations “false comfort.” “Logging back-to-back months above 1,000 CVEs proves automated bug-hunting has permanently reset patch volume,” he told The Register . “With AI making patch-diffing and exploit generation near-instant, the threat window opens the minute these updates drop.” For defenders, this means two things, Childs added. “What defenders need to know and do right now is abandon broad triage and take immediate defensive action: patch Exchange and Domain Controllers (LDAP/Kerberos) first to stop zero-click compromise, ring-fence exposed network services like DNS and DHCP to prevent wormable spread, and verify manual administrative fixes on your cloud services,” he said. Zero-click threats There are two zero-click threats in this month’s batch of fixes: CVE-2026-116928 and CVE-2026-119958 . Both are critical, carrying 9.8 CVSS ratings, in part because they don’t require any user interaction to exploit. CVE-2026-116928 is an out-of-bounds write in Microsoft Windows Search Component that could lead to remote code execution. An unauthenticated attacker could abuse this search feature in Exchange “by sending an email containing a specially crafted attachment,” Redmond warned. “Exchange automatically processes the attachment for indexing, so the recipient does not need to open the email or attachment. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the permissions of the affected processing service.” CVE-2026-119958 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Windows' implementation of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely without user interaction. This one can be exploited by sending specially crafted LDAP requests to vulnerable systems, potentially compromising domain controllers. Childs also counts 30 CVEs that pose a “wormable risk,” requiring zero authentication and zero user interaction over a network.…

articles.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
articles.content: When you deploy an agent to production, one of the hardest questions is whether it’s actually working? The bar isn’t whether it runs. It’s whether it does what the business needs, at scale. Many teams will tell you they can’t really see this. They spot-check outputs, watch latency, and collect user feedback when they can get it. None of that tells you whether the agent finished the user’s task, stayed on topic across a long session, leaked personally identifiable information (PII), or quietly skipped half the steps it was supposed to follow. Figure 1: Teams usually watch surface signals, but business outcomes are decided by the agent behaviors below the waterline Agent evaluation solves this problem. What makes this challenging is that a good score on one metric can hide a failure on another. A support agent can resolve every ticket and still expose personal information in its replies. In this case, the agent is failing although it has a high completion rate. To get evaluation right, measure the behaviors that matter for each agent, at the right level of detail. This post shows how to do this on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We use the AgentCore built-in evaluators together with the DeepEval and AutoEval evaluators directly from AgentCore Evaluations. Start with business outcomes, instead of metric names The most common mistake is to start with the metric list and pick the names that sound right. “Helpfulness sounds good, so we use it.” The result runs and produces numbers, but it gives almost no useful insight. The metric fits its label, not what success means for the agent. Instead, start with three steps. Define success in business terms. For a customer support agent, that might be first-contact resolution. For a research agent, it might be producing a complete, well-sourced answer grounded entirely in retrieved documents. For a content moderation assistant, it means flagging everything that should be flagged and only what should be flagged. Break the outcome into observable behaviors. A customer support agent that achieves first-contact resolution will typically complete the user’s stated goal, stay coherent across turns when the issue requires clarification, keep responses within compliance boundaries, and correctly invoke backend tools like ticket creation or order lookup. Map each behavior to an evaluator at the right level. Trace-level metrics cover per-turn or per-tool-call behaviors. Session-level metrics cover outcomes that only make sense when you look at the whole conversation. Figure 2: Translating a business outcome into observable behaviors and then into specific evaluators at the trace or session level This three-step process is the mental model that makes evaluation useful. The rest of this post is about what AgentCore gives you to execute it. The evaluator catalog AgentCore has a broad catalog of evaluators from three sources: Built-in evaluators are authored and quality-tested by AWS. You reference them by their ID ( Builtin.GoalSuccessRate , Builtin.Helpfulness , and 13 more) and the service handles everything else. They are benchmarked for reliability and cover the common dimensions, so they are the straightforward place to start. Third-party managed evaluators come from DeepEval and AutoEval , two established open-source evaluation libraries. When you use them in managed mode, AgentCore hosts the code, picks the judge model, and runs inference on its own capacity, exactly like built-in evaluators. If your team already uses one of these libraries in development, you can run the same metrics in production without a separate evaluation service. Custom evaluators take a built-in or third-party evaluator as a base, so you can swap in your own model and modify the prompt or rubric. Figure 3: The three evaluator tiers trade AWS quality assurance for increasing control over the model and account that run inference After creation, a custom derived evaluator is used exactly like other ones. The evaluator landscape…

articles.title: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
articles.content: Amazon is betting that many Ring customers will also want an AI-powered security drone and robot patrolling their homes or offices. But the company’s upcoming Ring Robotic products are also certain to intensify privacy concerns previously raised around a prior Amazon attempt to popularize a flying security camera. The Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam are expected to reach customers starting at the end of 2026 and in early 2027, respectively, according to an Amazon announcement posted on November 10. Amazon describes the devices as relying on an AI Pilot system that uses each device’s cameras along with “specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing” to plan patrol routes while autonomously navigating around obstacles such as furniture. Both devices also use that AI Pilot system to digitally map the floor plan of the customer’s home or business. This setup process occurs after the customer carries the Ring drone through their indoor spaces or allows the Ring Rover to do some autonomous exploration. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Your MRR Has a Ceiling, and Churn Sets It
articles.content: A common story among solo SaaS founders goes like this. Growth is steady for a year. Then it slows, then it stalls, even though signups have not dropped. The founder concludes that marketing has stopped working and starts looking for a new channel. Very often marketing is working exactly as well as before. The business has simply reached the ceiling its churn rate allows, and no new channel changes where that ceiling is unless it changes one of two numbers. The Formula Each month, two things happen to your monthly recurring revenue. New customers add some amount, call it N . Existing customers cancel, removing a share of current MRR equal to your monthly churn rate, c . next month's MRR = this month's MRR + N - (c × this month's MRR) Early on, N is much bigger than the churn loss, so MRR climbs. But the churn loss grows with MRR, while N stays roughly flat. Eventually they meet. When the amount you lose each month equals the amount you add, MRR stops moving: N = c × MRR MRR ceiling = N ÷ c Your MRR ceiling is the new MRR you add each month divided by your monthly churn rate. A Worked Example Say you add $600 of new MRR every month and lose 4% of your MRR to churn each month. ceiling = $600 ÷ 0.04 = $15,000 You will never get past $15,000 MRR with those two numbers, no matter how long you wait. Here is how you approach it, starting from zero: Month MRR Share of ceiling 6 $3,259 22% 12 $5,809 39% 24 $9,369 62% 36 $11,550 77% 60 $13,705 91% Two things stand out. Growth looks healthy for the first year, then slows every month after, without anything changing in the business. And at 4% monthly churn, you lose about 39% of your customers every year, which is why the curve bends so early. Why the Plateau Fools People The slowdown is gradual, so it looks like a trend in the market rather than a property of your numbers. Month to month, the gain shrinks: monthly gain = N - (c × MRR) At $5,000 MRR, you gain $600 - $200 = $400. At $10,000 you gain $600 - $400 = $200. At $14,000 you gain $40. Same signups, same marketing, ever-smaller net growth. Before you change channels, run the check: Add up the new MRR from the last three months and divide by three. That is N. Work out your average monthly churn rate over the same three months. That is c. Divide N by c. If your current MRR is already close to that number, more of the same marketing will not move you much. You are not stalling; you are arriving. Two Ways to Raise the Ceiling The formula only has two inputs, so there are only two levers. Raise N. Double your new MRR to $1,200 a month, and the ceiling doubles to $30,000. You can do it with more customers, or with the same number of customers at a higher price. A price rise counts here: if churn does not change, raising the price of new plans raises N, and the ceiling moves with it. Lower c. Halve churn to 2%, and the ceiling also doubles, to $30,000. But the two levers are not equivalent, because lowering churn changes how fast you get there. Month MRR at 4% churn MRR at 2% churn 12 $5,809 $6,458 24 $9,369 $11,527 36 $11,550 $15,504 60 $13,705 $21,073 At 4% churn, you reach half your ceiling in about 17 months. At 2% it takes about 34 months, because the ceiling is twice as high and you are filling it at the same rate. Lower churn is the bigger prize, but it is a slow one. The first year looks almost identical. Which Lever a Solo Founder Should Pull For a one-person business, the levers cost very different things. Raising N through acquisition usually costs time or money every single month, forever. Stop the marketing and N falls, and so does the ceiling. Lowering churn tends to be a one-off fix that keeps paying: an onboarding step that gets new users to the useful part faster, annual plans, a cancellation flow that offers a pause instead of an exit, fixing the bug that makes your most active users leave. Each of those keeps working after you stop thinking about it. Raising the price is the one move that raises N without more…

articles.title: iFixit's PROLED MacBook Pro Teardown Reveals Logo LEDs
articles.content: iFixit today took apart Apple's touchscreen PROLED MacBook Pro to see how Apple shed weight, what powers the logo, and how it compares to the 14-inch M6 ‌MacBook Pro‌. Apple added a glowing logo on the back of the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌, but since there's no backlight to illuminate it, Apple used four LEDs, a reflective layer, and a diffuser to create an even glow. When the light is off, the logo's two-way mirror coating gives it a shiny finish. Getting to the logo for repairs isn't easy because it's behind the display, so if it breaks, the only repair option is removing the screen. iFixit ended up breaking the panel because the glass separated from the layers underneath, destroying the OLED . Apple says the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ has a hinge designed for touch, but iFixit said it's basically identical to the M6 ‌MacBook Pro‌'s hinge, just stiffer, so it better holds its angle when the display is tapped at the top. The Thunderbolt/USB-C ports and fans are replaceable, but the logic board has to come out. The HDMI port and SDXC card slot are soldered to the logic board, so they're not as easily replaced. The SSD and memory are also soldered. iFixit swapped logic boards between two PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ models, and after running Repair Assistant, all of the components worked, including the touchscreen and Touch ID . iFixit said the touchscreen didn't add any new parts pairing problems. The PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌'s trackpad is a little bit smaller than the M6 model's, and weight was shed by removing some aluminum from the lower chassis. The lower case weighs 364 grams vs. 456 grams for the M6 model. The display assembly is 101 grams lighter despite the touchscreen and the glowing Apple logo, and the battery is two grams lighter too. The PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ earned a repairability score of 5 out of 10, which is a point higher than the M5 ‌MacBook Pro‌ and a point below the MacBook Neo . articles.title: New York Launches Nation's First State AI Testing Program
articles.content: New York is launching a state-backed AI safety research center at Binghamton University that will independently study and test AI systems, develop safety and security techniques, and train researchers in responsible AI. "While the federal government fails to act, New York is leading the way on AI safety and holding big tech accountable," New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said. "The stakes are too high to simply take AI companies at their word." Politico reports: The center -- which is funded by a $30 million gift from Bloomberg co-founder Tom Secunda and a $25 million research investment from SUNY and New York state -- is set to launch before New York's major AI safety law, the RAISE Act, comes into effect on Jan. 1. That will require submissions of detailed safety frameworks from AI companies operating in New York State, which Hochul's office hopes will be scrutinized by researchers at the new center. "AI is opening up questions that scientists could not tackle before," said Secunda, who also serves as the board chair of Empire AI, a $500 million public-private partnership. "With Empire AI and researchers across New York, the Center can test systems independently and give public officials evidence they can use." Over 80 leading scientists and researchers on AI systems from across New York state will contribute to the effort, which will be run by the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at Binghamton University, according to details shared by Hochul's office. The initiative will be led by Jeannette Wing, the executive vice president for research at Columbia University, and Greg Morrisett, the vice provost of Cornell Tech. "We need new techniques that can be applied to this new kind of system with swarms of autonomous agents acting independently and without control. How can you first detect that they're going to do harm, and how can you prevent them from doing harm?" said Wing. "The beauty of what's being proposed is that this state is committing resources to really light this up." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: How I Learned to Share Ownership With My Product Manager
articles.content: Building a creative partnership takes more than putting two strong specialists on the same project. You can be a brilliant designer, an experienced analyst, or a product manager who seems to have an answer for everything. Working with other people can amplify your expertise—or make it surprisingly difficult to put it to use. I have spent seven years at Yandex, working alongside highly capable people. I have also watched misunderstandings between those people turn straightforward tasks into complicated negotiations. Expertise does not automatically make collaboration easier. Sometimes, it gives each person more reasons to believe they are right. I learned that lesson through a conflict I helped create. I thought I was helping. While working at Yandex Market, I often took the lead in my partnership with a product manager. I answered product questions, defended our decisions, and proposed alternatives. My partner seemed less experienced to me. He needed more time to gather his thoughts, while I was quick to jump into a discussion. So I decided, on behalf of both of us, that I would do the talking. From my perspective, I was helping us move faster. Eventually, we had a conflict. Through several conversations, I realized that taking over was making him less confident. He had fewer opportunities to explain his reasoning and demonstrate his expertise. I interpreted his hesitation as a reason to step in again. We discussed what each of us needed. He wanted to present and defend the product rationale himself. I wanted design considerations to have a meaningful place in the decisions. We changed how we approached product reviews, introduced regular one-on-ones, and became more attentive to each other’s needs within the project. The problem had never been a shortage of ideas. I had assumed that my way of contributing worked for both of us. Bringing the creative pair into product work. That experience made me revisit my earlier work in advertising agencies, where projects often revolved around a creative pair. Two specialists brought different strengths and developed ideas together. When the partnership worked, they could produce strong work quickly. I started applying that approach more deliberately to product management and design. Of course, a PM and designer are part of a larger team. Engineers, analysts, researchers, and other colleagues shape the outcome. But this particular partnership influences many early decisions: which problem to solve, what to explore, and what to test. I recognize three recurring patterns. These are working dynamics, not fixed personality types. The PM drives; the designer executes. The PM defines the problem, chooses a solution, and sets the pace. The designer joins when something needs to be drawn. Work moves forward, but the team uses only part of the designer’s expertise. Questions about usability and alternative approaches arrive too late to influence the direction. A useful change is to involve design while the problem is still being framed. The designer also needs to bring questions and proposals into that conversation. The designer drives; the PM recedes. The designer takes over framing, strategy, discussions, and presentations. The PM becomes less visible, while the designer accumulates responsibility. I know this pattern well. Important tasks can fall through the cracks: who is coordinating with stakeholders, checking business assumptions, or deciding the scope of a release? Clear ownership helps, provided both people respect it. If your partner owns part of a discussion, leave them time to respond— even when you already have an answer. Both people adapt. Each person can lead, question assumptions, and make room for the other’s expertise. The designer might help turn an abstract request into a concrete problem. The PM might bring evidence or constraints that change the design direction. Both need to be willing to adjust. A partnership cannot depend on one person doing all the adapting. Look beyond…

articles.title: Democrats oppose plan to stack FCC with Republicans, plan probes of Chairman Carr
articles.content: Senate Democrats today opposed President Trump's nominee for an open Federal Communications Commission seat, and criticized Republicans for moving to confirm a new commissioner during the period before Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027. Democrats also plan to use their majority next year to launch probes of FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. "After the American people last week overwhelmingly rejected the MAGA agenda, there is no justification for this committee to advance partisan nominees during the lame-duck period," Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.) said today at the Commerce Committee's nomination hearing for Danielle Thumann Severs, Trump's pick to fill an empty commissioner's seat. Thumann Severs, an attorney and senior counsel to Carr, faced questions from Democrats about whether she supports Carr's attacks on TV broadcasters. Read full article Comments
articles.author: Jon Brodkin
