articles.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.content: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google and Mozilla . Image: Shutterstock.com. Diorama by @zepp1969. November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Overall, 535 of the flaws addressed this month allow an attacker to elevate their privileges on a vulnerable device. This latest round of updates means Microsoft has shipped more than 5,100 security patches so far this year, a staggering number considering that a year ago Microsoft was averaging around 100 patches per month. Microsoft credits advances in artificial intelligence for helping to find (and fix) such a large volume of security bugs in recent months. Last month, Microsoft pushed more than 1,400 fixes. According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploitation: CVE-2026-124194 , a spoofing bug in Outlook. The advisory for CVE-2026-124194 says it affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and editions of Microsoft Office . Several other major software makers pushed security updates this week to fix critical weaknesses in their products. Apple on Monday released out-of-cycle security updates to fix at least nine vulnerabilities in iOS/iPadOS , macOS , watchOS and visionOS . Among the weaknesses reportedly fixed in Apple’s release include an iMessage flaw that could let a remote attacker join a group chat and receive its messages; the updates also fix a separate iMessage flaw that could let someone added to a group access messages sent before they joined. Lee Neely , an instructor at the SANS Institute , noted that Apple backported the fix to iOS 18. “I take notice when Apple releases fixes to more than two versions,” Neely wrote in a SANS newsletter today. “You really need to get to version 27.2.1 of their OSes and push folks who are holding onto devices which cannot run the current version. The best plan often involves setting an upgrade date for old hardware. Run through all your Apple devices and make sure everything is up to date, don’t assume the fixes went out automatically.” Google this week released Chrome version 157.0.8103.50 , which resolves nine security holes, including CVE-2026-125350 , the sixth zero-day vulnerability this year for Chrome (this bug also being patched in Chromium-based browsers like Edge). The latest Chrome version follows its November 3 release, which fixed 213 vulnerabilities. A new version of Mozilla Firefox out today ( Firefox 160 ) resolves almost 100 CVEs, about half of them high severity. Adobe today released patches for at least 110 vulnerabilities across a range of products, with nearly half of the flaws rated high severity. Adobe said there is no evidence any of the security holes it addressed this month are being actively exploited. Chris Goettl , vice president of product management at Ivanti , said it’s easy for security teams at large enterprises to feel overwhelmed by the volume and criticality of patches from Microsoft lately. But he notes that while some 95,000 vulnerabilities have been assigned CVEs this year across all vendors, only 217 have so far this year been added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list maintained by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). “Roughly four in ten of this year’s exploited vulnerabilities sit in operating systems, endpoint software, browsers, and server platforms, which a continuous patch strategy can…
articles.author: BrianKrebs

articles.title: Your Google account will lose its ability to unlock your Nintendo account next year
articles.content: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR Nintendo is discontinuing Google and Apple account linking. Once the change goes into effect, you’ll no longer be able to log into your Nintendo account with a Google or Apple account. The target end date is January 26, 2027, but the official end could be delayed “depending on the progress of the system change work.” From Grubhub to ArtStation, you can connect your account to your Google account to make logging in easier. You could even do this with your Nintendo account, but that will no longer be the case soon. Nintendo is putting an end to linking your account with Google or Apple accounts. A newly published support page reveals that Nintendo plans on discontinuing Google and Apple account linking. Once the change goes into effect, you’ll no longer be able to log into your Nintendo account with a Google or Apple account. Users are also losing the ability to create a Nintendo account using Google or Apple. Additionally, the game publisher is putting an end to the My Nintendo Platinum Points mission that rewards users for connecting their accounts.
articles.author: Ryan McNeal

articles.title: Ring robots ready to patrol paranoids’ pads
articles.content: If you didn't have any privacy concerns about slapping a Ring doorbell on your front door or putting Ring cameras inside, you'll love Amazon's newest offerings, which move around homes and businesses to capture views stationary cameras might miss. The house of Bezos announced the launch of Ring Robotics on Tuesday along with its first two products: a drone designed for indoor home security, and a wheeled robot with a telescoping camera mast for automated after-hours business patrols. Both are designed to proactively patrol spaces as well as respond to alerts from connected alarm systems and Ring-connected devices. According to Ring founder Jamie Siminoff, this is something customers actually want, as those stationary cameras just can’t quite see everywhere. “It’s not just a new category of security; it’s the beginning of a future where proactive, autonomous protection is something every home and every business can have,” Siminoff said. The consumer-focused Ring Drone Cam launches from its own charging dock that Amazon says keeps the thing “out of sight” when not in use, and when in flight is able to patrol a home by flying around pre-programmed routes to take in the sights with its 148-degree FOV, 2K camera that includes LED illumination for night patrols. Amazon says it can also respond to alerts from cameras, sensors, and alarm systems. The Ring Rover Cam, designed with businesses in mind, is sort of like a security Roomba that sports a camera on a telescoping mast that Amazon says can be programmed to certain heights to let it see over counters, shelves, and other workplace obstacles. The Rover can also perform 360-degree scans and includes a siren, lights, and two-way audio so you can yell at intruders who aren't dissuaded by its presence. The Rover streams and records video in up to 4K while moving or patrolling and is designed to make regular patrols of businesses during off hours. It can also detect people and respond to alerts from connected Ring devices. Of course, given that this is Ring we're talking about, these flying and free-wheeling cameras use Amazon's cloud for some processing, likely inviting privacy concerns about what footage and mapping data the company can access and retain. The Amazon-owned security tech firm has faced a number of privacy complaints over the years, some of which have resulted in multimillion-dollar settlements. Ring agreed to pay $5.8 million in a 2023 settlement with the FTC over allegations that employees and contractors improperly accessed customers' private videos and that the company failed to adequately protect accounts against unauthorized access – just imagine the privacy concerns raised by flying robots. More recently, the company took heat for partnering with surveillance outfit Flock Safety, a relationship which it has since canceled . Amazon/Ring also invited criticism for a Super Bowl ad earlier this year promoting a new feature called Search Party, which would remotely activate Ring cameras to search for lost pets, suggesting that Amazon had the ability, in theory, to use Ring cameras like a dystopian neighborhood surveillance network. Another Ring feature, Familiar Faces, which uses AI-powered facial recognition to identify people captured by compatible cameras, prompted a proposed class-action lawsuit filed in June. The complaint alleges that the feature collected biometric information from visitors and passersby without their consent. If we can’t have iRobot, we’ll do it with Ring Amazon abandoned its efforts to buy Roomba robot-vacuum maker iRobot in 2024, blaming regulatory scrutiny for the move. The FTC, under then-chair Lina Khan, examined the deal's potential effects on competition and consumer privacy, including concerns about the information Roombas collect while mapping customers' homes. European regulators, meanwhile, raised concerns that Amazon could use its marketplace to disadvantage rival robot vacuum makers. With this Ring move, Amazon is once again…

articles.title: Yes, government officials confirm, the Jensen Huang scandal is really, really bad
articles.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has found himself embroiled in a scandal involving an alleged affair, a suspected Chinese spy, and some of America’s most closely guarded technology. Not exactly your garden-variety corporate indiscretion. There’s a lot to worry about. Experts are concerned that Huang’s repeated calls to loosen restrictions on advanced chip exports to China may have been influenced by the relationship. The affair also raises questions about Nvidia’s dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer led by Alice Huang. The Commerce Department began investigating Megaspeed last year, the New York Times reported , but transferred the probe to the Justice Department after Nvidia reached out. One of the stranger twists in the still-unfolding scandal is that the Trump administration appears to have known about the relationship —and Alice Huang’s suspected ties to the Chinese government—for some time. Yet intelligence officials apparently never warned Jensen Huang, and Trump seems to be brushing off the scandal . Despite an FBI investigation, the president has called Nvidia’s CEO an “ honorable guy ” and says he believes Huang didn’t know Alice was a spy. Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, says it has “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised” and has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” But current and former government tech officials say the assurances from Trump and Nvidia’s board do little to dispel their concerns. “A sophisticated individual should not have fallen prey to these advances,” a senior government official who focuses on AI issues tells Fast Company . “Obvious targets for espionage” The concern extends beyond Jensen Huang’s call for U.S. regulators to clear advanced chips to China. It’s possible Alice Huang may have picked up classified information—anything Trump might have mentioned—from the Nvidia CEO, given his close relationship with the president, suggests David Nesting, a former White House AI and cybersecurity official. Alice Huang may have had access to Nvidia information, too. (CHIPS for America, the Commerce Department initiative overseeing federal investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, did not respond to Fast Company ’s request for comment.) “His home, office, electronic devices, and private and professional communications would all be attractive intelligence targets,” Nesting tells Fast Company. “China would be enormously interested in Nvidia’s intellectual property, technology, roadmaps, supply chain, and how they might circumvent their export controls.” People who have sensitive and classified information are supposed to protect that information, but also work with security officials and alert them to anyone who might be asking about it, says the senior government official. “This is not just personal foibles,” the official adds. “Nvidia’s power and integral role in AI means that all decisions made by Mr. Huang inure not only to Nvidia but to the AI industry.” The affair, and its corresponding national security implications, underscore the risks of concentrating so much of the AI industry in the hands of a single company. Nvidia controls an estimated 80% of the market for GPUs used in AI, according to the OECD. That dependence has, in effect, exposed the country to an “enormous single point of failure,” argues Varoon Mathur, who formerly worked on AI issues at the White House. “When so much depends on one company, that company and its leadership become obvious targets for espionage, coercion, and foreign interference,” he says. “The wake-up call we all need” Pamela Jennings, a former senior policy officer at the CHIPS Research and Development program , housed inside the National Institute of Standards and Technology, sees the immediate fallout as a corporate crisis for Nvidia’s board to address. But the scandal also raises broader questions about how the U.S.…

articles.title: Oura is acquiring medical AI chatbot startup Counsel Health
articles.content: Oura announced its quarterly earnings today and said it agreed to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, after adding the company's AI chatbot to its app earlier this year . Counsel Health calls itself an "AI-native primary care company," using the app to deliver AI-generated responses and insights based on users' health data reported from their wearables that can then proceed to a conversation with one of its in-house physicians. Oura says it expects the deal to close before the end of the year. articles.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
articles.content: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it. You had one job Research from security firm Claroc shows that the exposed data includes things like internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results, galley checklists from a celebrity cruise line, and employee names and ID numbers. Ironically, some of the sensitive data comes from two-dozen apps built by SpaceXSI (the name of the now-merged SpaceX and xAI) itself. A small sampling of the documents revealed in the SpaceXSI apps—Claroc found 24 of them—include an onboarding plan, marked confidential, for a new member of SpaceXSI’s enterprise sales team, a sales territory map of 594 accounts, internal system addresses for sales team tools, and advertising proposals. articles.title: Seattle mayor lifts pause and will expand police surveillance cameras with new safeguards
articles.content: A view toward Pioneer Square and downtown Seattle from Lumen Field. (GeekWire File Photo / Kurt Schlosser) Seattle will expand its police surveillance camera network to three more neighborhoods, Mayor Katie Wilson said Tuesday , ending a pause she put in place in March over privacy and civil liberties concerns. The move comes a day after NYU’s Policing Project released an independent audit of the Seattle Police Department’s Real Time Crime Center (RTCC), which Wilson commissioned during the pause. The audit found the city had built “an important foundation” for overseeing the system but that “significant policy gaps remain.” It made 19 recommendations. Cameras in the Stadium District, installed before this summer’s FIFA World Cup, will be turned on immediately, according to the mayor’s office. Cameras around Garfield High School and in the Capitol Hill nightlife district still need to be bought and installed, which will take months. The City Council approved all three areas in 2025. Wilson briefly turned on the 22 stadium-area cameras during the World Cup, citing “credible threats” reported by law enforcement, and said they would go off after the tournament. The audit noted that police streamed live feeds throughout the event, despite a department policy against monitoring cameras without an active call or case. “After reviewing the evidence, the recommendations, and the safeguards available to us, I believe there is an important and responsible role for the RTCC within Seattle’s public-safety system,” Wilson said in a statement. Wilson said the city will adopt most of the audit’s recommendations. The police department will publish a public dashboard on how the crime center is used and tighten its rules on data retention, permissible uses and requests from outside agencies. A new advisory group will help write policies for privately owned cameras, protests and where future cameras go. No Flock cameras in Seattle, ever. New protections against potential abuses drawn from an outside audit. A handful of cameras in new neighborhoods. Here's what the RTCC looks like from the inside. pic.twitter.com/QeYUg8ZkW3 — Mayor Katie Wilson (@MayorofSeattle) November 10, 2026 The Real Time Crime Center, which launched in 2025 , pulls live video from hundreds of cameras into a single command room at police headquarters. They include 303 police-owned cameras at 61 sites, 116 security cameras at police buildings, 96 city traffic cameras, and 23 cameras owned by three local businesses that share their feeds with police. Analysts watch 911 calls as they come in and pull up nearby cameras to give officers details callers may have missed, such as what a suspect is wearing or which way they ran. They also comb through recorded footage to help detectives investigate past crimes. The system runs on Fusus, software from Axon, the Arizona-based maker of police body cameras and Tasers. Police are barred from using facial recognition with the system. The software does include an AI tool that searches video for people, vehicles and other objects, but analysts told auditors they use it only as a last resort because it is unreliable. In one case, a search for a man in a gray top and gray pants returned an image of a pigeon. Whether the system reduces crime remains an open question. The Seattle Police Department has said officers and detectives are three times more likely to make an arrest with help from crime center analysts, and that the center assisted in 17 homicide cases in 2025, helping close 10. But the audit notes that the department counts any analyst action as “support,” such as checking a camera, even if it produced nothing useful. Broader research on crime centers is thin, the audit found, and studies of surveillance cameras on their own show mixed results. A University of Pennsylvania evaluation of Seattle’s program, commissioned by the city’s inspector general, isn’t expected until late 2027. Live camera feeds as seen in the Seattle Police…

articles.content: Sony has canceled Fairgames , a heist game announced in 2023 , according to Bloomberg . Fairgames had once been part of Sony's big planned push for PlayStation live service games, but the company ended up canceling some planned live service titles, including in the God of War and The Last of Us franchises, and it shut down Concord shortly after its failed launch . articles.title: Anthropic Launches New Workplace Features To Take On Microsoft and Google
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from TechCrunch: Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets. The launch of Anthropic's new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks. Here's a summary of each of the offerings Anthropic announced today: Claude Meetings: Allows Claude to join video calls as a visible participant, take notes, answer questions, retrieve information from connected apps, and create plans, timelines, and action items in real time. Available in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, initially supporting Google Meet. Claude Whiteboards: A collaborative visual workspace where teams can brainstorm with Claude, organize ideas into timelines and plans, and turn their work into documents or slide decks. It also integrates with Claude Meetings to build whiteboards during conversations. Claude Sheets: Lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude, including budgets and trackers with multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude can make changes directly in cells while explaining its edits. Anthropic also announced the general availability of Claude Data (formerly Claude Dashboards) that connects Claude to business systems like CRMs and data warehouses. "Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos," reports TechCrunch. Additionally, the company announced new interactive connectors that let users open Claude and work within third-party apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: To thwart reverse engineering by agents, dev proposes blinding them
articles.content: Now that LLMs can help analyze commercial software binaries and recreate their functionality, one software developer and student has created a project designed to make this process more difficult. Timo Zhang's project is called Blind LLM Agents (BLA), and as its name suggests, it attempts to interfere with efforts by AI agents to scrutinize app code. "Coding agents can reverse-engineer shipped packages, CLIs, and WASM in minutes," Zhang told The Register in an email. "Classic obfuscation was built for humans and static tools, not LLMs that reason about meaning. Blind LLM Agents is a protection layer for that threat model." Such agents can also help developers build alternatives to existing commercial software. Last month, Artcraft , a two-person development shop, released seven open-source apps that aim to be replacements for Adobe's commercial apps Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. Artcraft claims these apps are "clean-room reimplementations" written from scratch in Rust using Anthropic Opus 5.5. Setting aside the question of whether enlisting an AI model to reimplement an app really immunizes the creator from legal risk, those making apps face the possibility that someone will have an LLM probe published app binaries and reconstruct them through reverse engineering. There's in fact a framework for this, Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). Zhang has faced some criticism on social media for creating a limited barrier to copying other people's work (which at this point might simply be the work of another LLM). But not everyone accepts that all publicly accessible binaries should be easily available for review and reuse. BLA cannot prevent committed reverse engineering efforts, but it may add a bit of friction to the process when LLMs are involved. "It doesn't write app code — it hardens what you've already built," Zhang said. "A transform pipeline (plus MCP tools / an agent Skill) applies renaming, lane splitting, seed-derived string encryption, build polymorphism, WASM export renaming, decoys, self-seal integrity checks, and a coverage matrix that won't claim protection it can't prove. Behavior stays equivalent; recovery cost goes up." Zhang said various evaluations like red teaming and CrackMe challenges to recover keys or flags from hardened artifacts show that BLA is effective. "We also drive REA (a reverse-engineering agent) against those builds," he said. "Fail-to-break is the pass. CI tracks defense score, self-verifies integrity coverage, and checks functional equivalence. We raise the cost — we don't claim it is unbreakable." The project website says as much, noting that it raises the effort for analysis and adds decoy code, but doesn't promise protection against traditional interactive reverse engineering tools like Ghidra or Frida. Zhang said he's aware of other software projects that aim to interfere with AI, such as Poison Fountain for poisoning training data and Anubis for deterring bots and scraping. BLA, he said, is different. It's for hardening shipping code against reverse engineering and LLM-aided analysis. ®
articles.author: Thomas Claburn

articles.title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
articles.content: Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called "big math" is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend. Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. In 2005, Strogatz extended his study of synchronicity to the crowds that caused the wobbling of London's Millennium Bridge . An award-winning communicator, Strogatz wrote three series of columns on mathematics for The New York Times in 2010, 2012, and 2025 and hosted a podcast for Quanta magazine from 2020–2021. He has written four popular books: Sync (2003), The Calculus of Friendship (2009), The Joy of X (2012), and the New York Times bestseller Infinite Powers (2019). Read full article Comments

articles.title: Apple's 'Harbor' app will make running local AI across multiple Macs trivial
articles.content: An app presently called "Harbor" will help turn multiple Macs into a private AI inference server, keeping data local while also making the process of creating an AI server much easier. The Mac Studio is great for AI work The Mac has become a very useful tool for AI research, but it could be even more useful. Apple is working on an app that can make it easier to run large language models (LLMs) locally, so long as you have enough processing power and memory available. Formerly known as Fabric, Harbor is the app that creates a private AI inference server on a Mac, according to Aaronp613 on X. It is capable of running open-weight models on the Mac itself, and apparently is extremely user-friendly. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums
articles.author: Malcolm Owen <malcolm@appleinsider.com>

articles.title: Apple Releases New AirPods Firmware
articles.content: Apple today released new firmware for the AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3 , AirPods 4, AirPods 5 , and AirPods Max 2 . The firmware has a build number of 9B47, up from 9A348/9A350. Apple has been beta testing the new firmware for the last several weeks, but hasn't yet offered details on what's included in the software. Apple has an AirPods support document that it will update with information soon. Firmware updates can be downloaded by connecting the AirPods to an Apple device and connecting them to power. It can take a few hours for new firmware to be installed because there is no software update option like there is for other Apple devices. articles.title: One Prompt, Every Log: Triage Production Issues Faster with MCP
articles.content: Production issues aren't painful because fixing bugs is hard. They're painful because finding where the bug originated can take hours. This is where MCP (Model Context Protocol) comes in. MCP is an open standard that allows AI assistants to connect with external tools and data sources, such as databases, monitoring platforms, application logs, and project management tools. It enables AI to interact with these systems and gather the context needed to investigate complex issues. Hi I'm Shakti, a Software Engineer at a bug healthcare company. Recently I've been working closely with production issues and I've realized one thing time is everything when dealing with production incidents. The real challenge isn't just fixing the bug. It's identifying where it originated, performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and reproducing the issue in lower environments. All these steps can be extremely time-consuming. But don't worry, I've got you! Here are some practical tips on how you can use AI to triage production issues faster, identify root causes, and save valuable debugging time. Step 1: Identify and Collect All the MCP Tools We Need Start by identifying all the tools you manually use while triaging production issues. For example: Database MCP: Investigate database records and validate data. Make sure you have read-only access . Grafana / New Relic MCP: Analyze l, dashboards, and application performance. Browser Developer Tools MCP: Inspect network requests, API responses, and browser console errors. CloudWatch / Azure Logs MCP: Investigate application and infrastructure logs. Jira / Rovo MCP: Fetch ticket details, comments, requirements, and related issues. Basically think about every tool you manually open when investigating a production issue and check whether an MCP is available for it. Step 2: Verify Permissions and Access Having an MCP integration doesn't automatically mean you have access to everything. Check whether your account has the required permissions to access these tools, especially production databases, monitoring dashboards, application logs, and Jira projects. Make sure you follow your organization's security and access policies. Prefer read-only access wherever possible. Step 3: Connect Everything to Your AI Harness Once you've identified the required MCP servers and verified your permissions, connect them to your primary AI harness or the AI assistant you use daily. For example, this could be Claude, Cursor, or another AI environment that supports MCP integrations. Step 4: Verify Your Integrations Now that you've connected all the tools, verify that your AI assistant can actually communicate with them. Test a few basic operations: Can it fetch Jira tickets? Can it query the database? Can it retrieve application logs? Can it access Grafana or New Relic metrics? Don't move forward until you've verified that the integrations are working as expected. Step 5: Create a Dedicated Project for Production Issue Triage This is where things get interesting! Create a separate project in your AI harness specifically for production issue triaging. Give this project a detailed system prompt that defines the AI's role as an experienced Production Support Engineer who understands debugging, root cause analysis, log investigation, and issue reproduction. Your instructions should tell the AI to: Understand the production issue from the Jira ticket. Identify the affected services, APIs, and components. Investigate relevant application logs and monitoring metrics. Check database records wherever relevant and permitted. Identify potential root causes using the available evidence. Suggest ways to reproduce the issue in lower environments. Correlate findings across different tools. Generate a concise investigation report containing findings, supporting evidence, probable root cause, and recommended next steps. articles.title: Anthropic wants Claude to be the front end for your entire enterprise app stack
articles.content: Anthropic is expanding Claude’s ability to work directly inside enterprise applications; it can now open full software interfaces, retrieve information, and make changes without requiring users to move between applications. At The Briefing: Work at the Frontier in San Francisco on Tuesday, the company announced expanded interactive connectors, along with new tools for meetings, spreadsheets, shared workspaces, and business data. “For years, we’ve learned to work around software. Now Claude works around you,” said Ami Vora , Anthropic’s chief product officer, in remarks prepared for the event. “For years, we’ve learned to work around software. Now Claude works around you,” Full apps open inside Claude Anthropic’s interactive connectors previously let users see a small preview of a connected app in Claude. Now, they can open and work in the full application within the conversation, starting with Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot. For example, Claude can edit a Confluence page directly or update an Adobe design using assets from a company’s brand kit. Users do still need to approve those changes before Claude executes. Built on MCP Apps The expanded connectors are built on MCP Apps , which lets MCP servers provide interactive interfaces instead of relying solely on tool calls. Developers can bring existing application interfaces into Claude using app tools and embedded websites, without rebuilding them for the assistant. The new capabilities are in public preview and aren’t limited to Claude, since other AI clients that support MCP Apps can use them too. The new capabilities are in public preview and aren’t limited to Claude, since other AI clients that support MCP Apps can use them too. Anthropic says Claude Marketplace now includes more than 9,000 connectors and plugins, continuing the effort to connect AI systems with enterprise infrastructure . For applications without a supported connector, Claude can use its built-in browser to interact with them. Existing permissions still apply The company says connectors respect the permissions employees already have in the underlying application. For example, a user who cannot access a particular Google Drive document cannot retrieve it through Claude. Administrators can also restrict individual connector capabilities, including allowing Claude to read Slack messages without permission to send messages. Additionally, Anthropic is introducing Claude auto-connect in beta, a ten-minute setup that lets administrators enable connectors across an organization without requiring employees to configure them individually. Smart Reports, meanwhile, gives administrators visibility into team usage, completed work, and spending. Claude Data gets certified queries Anthropic is also making Claude Data generally available, following its October launch as Claude Dashboards . The update introduces certified queries, allowing data teams to approve the queries Claude uses for reporting so different teams get consistent numbers from the same data. The update introduces certified queries, allowing data teams to approve the queries Claude uses for reporting so different teams get consistent numbers from the same data. A second feature, live sharing, lets employees access updated dashboards without needing direct access to the underlying data source. Both features are still in beta. Anthropic hasn’t detailed how it handles versioning for certified queries or changes to the source data’s schema. Task delegation moves beyond engineering Claude Meetings, which Anthropic says is coming soon, will join video calls to create project plans, answer questions, and retrieve information from connected applications. The feature is planned for Team and Enterprise customers but won’t be available to organizations using zero data retention, HIPAA-ready configurations, or customer-managed encryption keys. The milestone comes a week after Mercedes sold its 47 European charging hubs to France’s Electra. Mercedes-Benz’s fast-charging network in North America has reached 100 sites three years after opening its first station, InsideEVs reported. […] This story continues at The Next Web

articles.title: Google’s November Pixel update packs dozens of bug fixes, and you can get it now
articles.content: TL;DR Alongside the new functionality debuting with the November Pixel Drop, Google’s got its latest batch of Pixel bug fixes to deliver. In addition to dozens of fixes impacting the current Pixel lineup, we’ve also got a few unique to newer and older Pixel hardware. OTA downloads are available now for users interested in sideloading. Google just announced its November Pixel Drop , delivering new features and expanding access to old ones across the Pixel lineup, but that’s just that half of it — we’re also getting the latest set of monthly fixes and stability improvements. Our most recent monthly Pixel update may be a week behind its normal schedule , but today Google’s correcting that oversight with the formal announcement of its November 2026 Pixel update, available for Pixel 6a and newer hardware. As Google’s Mishaal Rahman confirms over on Reddit, this release marks the arrival of Android 17 QPR2.
articles.author: Stephen Schenck

articles.title: One Identity Unveils Safeguard 9.0 for Simpler PAM
articles.content: Alisa Vijeo, California, November 10th, 2026/CyberNewswire/-- One Identity today unveiled Safeguard 9.0, a major update designed to reduce the infrastructure, administrative overhead and operational complexity associated with enterprise privileged access management. As privileged access management becomes more critical and complex, One Identity Safeguard continues to advance around a straightforward goal: make enterprise-grade privileged access easier for administrators and users to manage. The current One Identity documentation identifies Safeguard for Privileged Passwords 9.0 and Safeguard for Privileged Sessions 9.0 as the latest major releases. The Safeguard 9.0 upgrades include a move to hardware-agnostic deployment, Windows 11 LTSC with embedded licensing for Safeguard for Privileged Passwords, and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS for Safeguard for Privileged Sessions. Software updates are also designed to install faster with less disruption, while session management no longer requires a separate license file simply to continue operating. See the documented Safeguard 9.0 upgrades. Safeguard 9.0: Streamlined workflows reduce administrative friction The usability improvements extend directly into privileged-access operations. Safeguard 9.0 introduces asset-scoped just-in-time group elevation, allowing group membership to be elevated for an individual request and removed again without administrators creating additional accounts or groups. ESXi account discovery reduces manual tracking, while TLS 1.3 and configurable cipher selection make security policies easier to manage and demonstrate during audits. Review the Safeguard 9.0 feature additions . This emphasis on reducing operational complexity supports Safeguard's position among top privileged access management solutions . PeerSpot and Gartner reinforce Safeguard's momentum External customer research supports that story. PeerSpot lists Safeguard by One Identity among its top five PAM solutions , with an 8.6/10 rating based on 92 reviews. Its assessment highlights streamlined password management and compliance among the areas users value. At the analyst level, One Identity was positioned as a Challenger in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management . The One Identity page also reports a 4.7/5 Gartner Peer Insights rating from 200 verified reviews, with 94% saying they would recommend Safeguard. Feature in focus: Operational UX with Safeguard 9.0 Safeguard 9.0 is an operational UX upgrade: reducing infrastructure and licensing friction, shortening maintenance disruption and making just-in-time privileged access easier to administer. About One Identity One Identity delivers trusted identity security for enterprises worldwide to protect and simplify access to digital identities. With flexible deployment options and subscription terms – from self-managed to fully managed – our solutions integrate seamlessly into your identity fabric to strengthen your identity perimeter, protect against breaches, and ensure governance and compliance. Trusted by more than 11,000 organizations managing over 500 million identities, One Identity is a leader in identity governance and administration (IGA), privileged access management (PAM), and access management (AM) for security without compromise. One Identity is recognized as one of the best cybersecurity companies for agentic AI security and NHI management solutions. Users can learn more at www.oneidentity.com . Contact Ali Sayyed ali.sayyed@oneidentity.com This story was published as a press release by Cybernewswire under HackerNoon’s Business Blogging Program

One Identity is recognized as one of the best cybersecurity companies for agentic AI security and NHI management solutions. Users can learn more at www.oneidentity.com . articles.title: GTA 6 pre-loads begin today for PS5 — start downloading now and get ready for these big exclusive features
articles.content: Starting today (Nov. 10), if you've pre-ordered Grand Theft Auto 6 you can now preload the game, which demands up to 212GB of storage. If you got the code-in-a-box version you can preload that as soon as you get the box, according to PlayStation . This is a massive game, and you may need to tweak your system to run it. We've put together a guide to help you prepare your PS5 (or Xbox) before you preload the game. If you haven't yet pre-ordered GTA 6, you can still do so and once you've paid, you can immediately pre-load the game before the November 19 launch day. PS5 exclusives (Image credit: Sony) Speaking of Xbox, those of you on PlayStation might have a slight experiential advantage over those with Microsoft's console. Sony has a made a big deal of marking GTA 6 as "plays best on PS5," especially the PS5 Pro given all the power under the hood. Specifically, Rockstar highlighted PSSR and ray-traced shadows on the Pro console. "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro." Across the PS5 lineup, GTA 6 utilizes features like the DualSense's integrated speakers, haptic feedback and adaptive triggers to make the game more immersive. "Grand Theft Auto VI for PS5 includes high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D Audio, and improved load times, making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles." Sony claims the game loads faster thanks to the console's high-speed SSD; that is something we'll have to test and see if it's true. Xbox players do get to take advantage of Xbox Cloud Gaming, though the game will be streamed at Xbox Series S graphics settings, and could be hampered by connection speeds. The game is supposed to support remote play on both PlayStation and Xbox, so your Portal can get some serious use. If you've got the console handled, consider this essential GTA 6 gear for the ultimate GTA 6 setup. The cost of gaming Unfortunately, if you want to play on a PS5 Pro, availability is an ongoing concern. If you managed to get one at the launch price of $700, or the new $900 price, that's great, but now? Eesh. At the beginning of October, we reported that third-party sellers were trying to sell used PS5 Pros for over $1,400. Unfortunately, nothing has changed since then. The PS5 Pro is unavailable at most official retailers and the PlayStation Store. So the if you see one for sale it's most likely the third-party price. Honestly, you might still have your best luck on eBay — not that it'll be cheap. articles.title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
articles.content: Google has announced a " super network " upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it's adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one. Google's MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google's Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel. With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google's blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn't mention either network, saying only that it supports "two of America’s best 5G cellular networks." Read full article Comments

articles.title: DOJ sues Lyft for allegedly denying rides to people with disabilities
articles.content: The Justice Department has filed a lawsuit against Lyft , accusing the company of discriminating against passengers with disabilities who seek rides on its platform. The federal lawsuit, filed Monday, says Lyft “is aware of, but fails to prevent and remedy” several discriminatory practices against riders who need accommodations under the Americans With Disabilities Act. That includes denying rides to people who have service animals or use stowable wheelchairs and refusing to let passengers with mobility issues sit in the front seat, the suit alleges. “Individuals with disabilities should be able to rely on ride-share services free of discrimination,” said Jesus A. Osete, acting assistant attorney general, in a statement. “We intend to uphold the ADA’s promise that people with disabilities are entitled to equal access in every part of public life, including essential transportation services.” Lyft firmly rejected the accusations in a statement. The lawsuit is the latest from the federal government that targets ride-hailing companies for the treatment of would-be riders with disabilities. The administration filed a similar lawsuit against Uber last year, which is ongoing. Uber settled a separate suit in 2022, and Lyft settled a different one in 2020. The companies stress that their policies and in-app tools require that drivers provide ADA accommodations and remind them of the consequences of refusing to do so. The new lawsuit against Lyft named several examples of people across the country who hailed a ride on the platform but had one—or, in some cases, several—drivers refuse to take them to their destination, including as recently as last month. Those individuals experienced delays in getting to medical appointments, cancellation fees, and other issues as a result, the suit said. Lyft policies require drivers to accommodate riders who travel with service animals or mobility devices, and “drivers who violate these policies face serious consequences, including permanent deactivation,” the company said in a statement. “We’ve cooperated with the DOJ throughout its review and remain committed to serving every rider, including riders with disabilities,” the company said. The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. The Department of Justice said it is seeking $53 million for individuals who have been discriminated against and have submitted complaints to Lyft or the department. —By Hannah Fingerhut, Associated Press

articles.title: OffSec Celebrates 20 Years of Practitioner-Built Training From the Creators of Kali Linux and OSCP
articles.content: New York, USA, November 10th, 2026/CyberNewswire/--Kali Linux. OSCP. Try Harder. For 20 years, OffSec has set the standard for the tools security practitioners use, the skills they prove, and the mindset they bring to the work. This month OffSec is marking its 20th anniversary as a global leader in hands-on cybersecurity training and certifications for individuals and enterprise security teams. "Our founders built an incredible brand and an incredible product,” said OffSec CEO Ning Wang. “Our mission has stayed the same. We develop critical thinkers, cyber warriors, and problem solvers who are ready to excel in their jobs under stress. Hands-on is the only way we believe you can effectively train someone.” Built by the People Who Do the Work OffSec began in 2006 when cybercrime was becoming big business. OffSec grew out of the security community, founded by practitioners who believed the best way to teach cybersecurity was to share what they'd learned through hands-on experience. That origin story still shapes how OffSec develops cybersecurity practitioners and teams. Through hands-on training with real systems, learners build practical skills, strengthen their problem-solving abilities, and gain the confidence to tackle challenges when the obvious approach fails. The Tools Practitioners Use BackTrack Linux brought penetration testing tools together in one open-source platform. In 2013, OffSec rebuilt it as Kali Linux , a free environment for penetration testing, research, forensics, and reverse engineering. In 2023, Kali Purple extended it to defenders. The Standard Practitioners Prove Themselves Against OSCP earned its reputation as the gold standard in penetration testing certifications because candidates must work through live systems, adapt their approach, and document what they accomplish. Employers trust it as evidence of real capability. For many practitioners, it is a career-defining milestone. OSCP+ added a renewable credential in 2024. Now, for a limited time, individual practitioners can save 20% off of Learn One annual subscription. The Research and Practice They Learn From In 2009, OffSec launched the Exploit Database, a non-profit, public-service archive of public exploits, proof-of-concept (PoC) code, shellcode, and security papers, which it still maintains as a free resource. It also acquired the open-source training project VulnHub, offers free labs in Proving Grounds Play, and recently added HackTrack. HackTrack offers live weekly training over a 10-week stretch. The first round of HackTrack focused on OSCP and was offered free to those with a Learn One or Course and Certification Bundle. A new HackTrack focused on OSAI is set to launch soon. Along the way, Try Harder became the security community's shorthand for the persistence and dedication that a career in cybersecurity demands. In October 2026 at Singapore International Cyber Week, CEO Wang urged her Women in Cyber keynote audience to do hard things early that build confidence and resilience, noting, “If you don’t struggle through something, you will never become really great at it,” she said. The Technology Looks Different. The Challenge Feels Familiar Attackers now use AI to discover and weaponize vulnerabilities at speeds unimaginable 20 years ago. The time between a vendor patch and a working exploit continues to shrink. Cybersecurity skills gaps remain a growing challenge. According to ISC2’s 2025 Cybersecurity Workforce Study, 95% of organizations report at least one skills gap, with 59% describing those gaps as critical or significant, up from 44% in 2024. These findings reinforce the need to move beyond once-a-year training toward continuous, hands-on skill development, an approach rooted in OffSec’s philosophy since day one. “Frontier AI models are evolving at unbelievable speed. articles.title: Your Pixel just got a ton of new features — here's what dropped and how they work
articles.content: Google just announced its November Pixel Drop, which adds a slew of new features for Pixel phones and watches. Plus, the Pixel Tag officially goes on sale today (look out for our review here). There's a ton of stuff in the drop, but some highlights include expanded Gemini Intelligence, a new Create My Widget feature and step-by-step workouts on Pixel Watch 3 and newer. The company also announced its new Google Fi "Super Network." We've got more details about how it works here . Let's dive into what's available and which devices support these new features. Pixel Phones (Image credit: Tom's Guide / John Velasco) For the most part, the big features are only coming to the Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series phones in this update. Some smaller tools are available on Pixel 6 and later phones. Surprise, most of it is AI-related. Gemini Intelligence and AI (Image credit: Google) Starting with AI, Gemini Intelligence is now available on Pixel 10 phones, including the new Rambler feature, which automatically removes filler words and can format your spoken words into "clean, coherent" text. It also adds automations for specified apps, including grocery ordering, ridesharing and booking reservations. Create My Widgets enables you to build custom widgets using AI by describing the type of tool you need. Google is also offering curated recommendations. Gemini Call Screen is on Pixel 11 phones and screens calls on demand. For Pixel 10 and 11 phones, Gemini can make calls for you, doing things like checking inventory, putting items on hold, or making/changing reservations. Pixel 11 phones are getting Pixel Solver, which uses generative AI to create custom templates and "conversational, multi-step problem solving for everyday" math. Pixel 9 and above phones are getting Notification Summaries that will recap long conversations, giving you context at a glance. Non-AI features and older Pixels (Image credit: Tom's Guide) The highlight feature, pun intended, is HiLight, announced at the Made By Google event in August. When your phone is face down, HiLight will glow to let you know if a favorite contact has sent you a message. (Image credit: Google) Otherwise, for 6a and above, there's a new Custom Icons style, which uses Nano Banana to generate. Transit Mode 2.0 triggers automatically based on phone sensors. Pixel Search Updates lets you find content across your apps, web and settings using natural language search directly from the All Apps screen. Unit Conversion is a module to help you skip toggling between the browser and the calculator. Pixel 6 and above phones are also getting Live Location Sharing for Pixel VIPs. Finally, Pixel 10 phones are getting Extreme Charging Mode that quickly charges your phones to full. Pixel Watch features (Image credit: Toms Guide) Your Pixel Watch isn't getting as many features as the phones, but the big one is "Step-by-Step Workouts." Basically, your watch will give you step-by-step instructions for each exercise in your routine. It will also log reps, weights and track metrics from your Watch, or your phone. This is available on Pixel Watch 3 and newer models. Google announced that Create My Widgets, Gemini call Screen and Notification Summaries, outlined above, are "coming soon"; no specific date was provided. Phone to Watch Unlock is also coming soon to Pixel Watch 3 and new models. This feature will let you unlock your watch with a nearby paired phone. No date was provided here either. articles.title: HiLight on Pixel 11 Pro phones now supports Google Messages
articles.content: TL;DR Google introduced its HiLight notification light with Pixel 11 Pro models this year. So far, HiLight has officially supported Phone and WhatsApp calls, as well as Gemini interactions. That’s now expanding to also include Google Messages. Google brought Pixel phones a new hardware feature this year, marking the debut of the HiLight notification light on Pixel 11 models, and now, with the release of the November Pixel Drop, it’s picking up some new functionality. Notification lights have been around since phones weren’t even that smart, but in recent years we’ve seen less and less of them — which is a shame, because they can be genuinely useful. But while we were excited to see Google embrace them again for Pixel 11 phones (well, the Pro models, anyway), so far HiLight has been a little limited in terms of what it can officially do.

articles.title: Gboard’s Rambler voice typing expands to the Pixel 10 series
articles.content: TL;DR Gboard’s Rambler voice typing feature is now available on the Pixel 10, 10 Pro, 10 Pro XL, and 10 Pro Fold. Rambler is designed to make sense of your speech by blocking out filler words and providing a polished block of text. The feature has been exclusive to the Pixel 11 series so far, though the third-party app PixelBoard has unofficially unlocked access on other Android devices. Gboard’s latest voice dictation feature, Rambler , is coming to Pixel 10 phones. This feature, which has remained exclusive to the Pixel 11 lineup, is now expanding to cover the company’s 2025 flagships. In addition to Rambler, Google is also bringing a few other Gemini Intelligence features to the Pixel 10 series as part of the November Pixel Drop. With this expansion, Rambler in Gboard is now available on the Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, and the Pixel 10 Pro Fold in all regions and languages, joining the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold.

articles.title: Pixel 11’s better Pixel Search is expanding to every Pixel launched since 2021
articles.content: Credit: Prakhar Khanna / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s Pixel Search app, launched with the Pixel 11, is coming to older phones. All phones, including Pixel 6 and newer, now support the refreshed Search experience. Pixel Search goes beyond traditional Google Search on Android devices, letting users look for files, folders, conversations, Drive, Photos, calendar entries, and more using natural language. The November 2026 Pixel Drop is here, and along with several new features for the broad Pixel lineup, it also expands Pixel 11-exclusive items to older phones. One such feature is the renewed Pixel Search experience , which first arrived with the Pixel 11 series. Now, Google is expanding it to older phones, going all the way back to the Pixel 6 series. The persistent search bar on Pixel phones’ home screens has long offered an experience that is distinct from the rest of Android devices. Unlike other Android devices, search on Pixel phones has traditionally also brought up results from local files and apps alongside web search results. Last year, Google temporarily took that away , but only to introduce an even more far-reaching Pixel Search app when it launched the Pixel 11 phones.

articles.title: Google’s November Pixel Drop brings over 12 new features, and Pixel 10 owners are the big winners
articles.content: Google has announced its November Pixel Drop, and this time, it’s a busy one. The update starts rolling out today, November 10, to all supported Pixel phones, tablets, and smartwatches. It brings a handful of genuinely new tools, including an AI-powered math solver in the Calculator app and a long-awaited widget builder that works from natural language prompts. Pixel Tag, first announced alongside the Pixel 11 series, is also now officially available. Meanwhile, Pixel 10 owners are getting a big chunk of the Gemini Intelligence features that launched with the Pixel 11 series , including Rambler and Gemini’s task automations. Several other features are also expanding to older Pixels and new regions.

articles.title: Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop
articles.content: Google's Pixel phones get an update every month, but most are just security patches and bug fixes. The bigger changes are bundled into quarterly Pixel Drops, and one is rolling out today . The update brings a few new things, and many of the Gemini features previously exclusive to the latest Pixel phones will also expand to Google's Pixel 10 lineup. The Pixel 11 was Google's first foray into "Gemini Intelligence" branding, something we'll see a lot more of going forward. Some of the features under that heading were limited to Google's newest phones (and in some cases, Samsung's phones). The November Pixel Drop will expand these AI features to the Pixel 10 lineup, but importantly, that doesn't include the budget-oriented Pixel 10a . For starters, the Pixel 10 series will get the improved personalized suggestions (previously known as Magic Cue) that debuted on the Pixel 11 . This enables things like sending grocery lists to Google Keep from other apps and generating summaries from the context menu. Rambler, Google's AI-assisted voice input system, is also coming to the 2025 phones. Likewise, Gemini app automation will roll out on Pixel 10 with this update. This feature is still limited to select apps in rideshare, food delivery, travel, and a few other categories. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Speech Processing Pioneer Bishnu Saroop Atal Dies at 93
articles.content: Bishnu Saroop Atal Acoustics and signal processing pioneer Life Fellow, 93; died 19 August Atal was an acoustics and signal processing researcher at Bell Labs in Murray Hill, N.J., and later at AT&T ’s Shannon Laboratory, in Florham Park, N.J. His pioneering work on voice-coding techniques became the foundation for efficient, high-quality voice transmission over cellular networks. He received the 2013 IEEE Jack S. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “fundamental and pioneering contributions to speech coding.” He joined Bell Labs in 1961 as a communications researcher, and his early work there focused on speaker identification technology. During the 1960s he helped develop linear predictive coding , a powerful method for analyzing and compressing speech. LPC is now the most widely used method for encoding speech at a low bit rate. Atal developed increasingly sophisticated low-bit-rate speech-coding techniques. They included multipulse LPC , which improved the quality of compressed speech. Bishnu Saroop Atal Nokia Bell Labs He also worked with his colleague Manfred R. Schroeder to develop code-excited linear prediction , a method for producing high-quality speech at very low bit rates. CELP became a foundational technique in modern speech coding, letting digital communications systems carry voice using less bandwidth. The extra efficiency expanded cellular capacity, allowing wireless networks to handle more simultaneous calls. Later in his career, he led the acoustics and speech research departments at Bell. The company named him a Fellow in 1994. When AT&T Bell Laboratories split into separate research organizations in 1996, Atal continued his career at the AT&T Florham Park headquarters, and he was named a Fellow the following year. He retired in 2002 and became an affiliate professor of electrical engineering at the University of Washington , in Seattle. There he continued his research in speech processing, speech recognition, and high-dimensional computing. Atal was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1987 and the National Academy of Sciences in 1993. He received numerous awards including the 2018 International Speech Communication Association Medal for Scientific Achievement and a 2003 medal from the Franklin Institute . He received a bachelor’s degree in physics in 1952 from the University of Lucknow , in India, and a master’s degree in 1955 in electrical engineering from the Indian Institute of Science , in Bengaluru. While working full time at Bell he earned a Ph.D. in EE in 1968 from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn (now New York University’s Tandon engineering school ), in New York City. Darryl Palmer Jr. Chair of the IEEE Central Illinois Section Senior member, 55; died 30 August Palmer was a dedicated IEEE volunteer, serving as chair of the Central Illinois Section and as the government relations chair of Region 4 . He was a member of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society and its industrial activity committee. He also served as associate editor of the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics . In 1986, at age 16, Palmer completed a summer internship at NASA’s Glenn Research Center , in Cleveland. He helped develop FoilSim , an interactive educational software program that introduces aerodynamic engineering to preuniversity students. While studying computer science at Cleveland State University in 1996, he joined the university’s Allen-Bradley PLC lab as a research assistant. He designed hardware and software systems for the Glenn Research Center to collect and process thermal wave imaging data. He also designed software for General Motors ’ North American robotic and welding division. In 1999 he completed a second internship at the research center and helped develop EngineSim , an educational software program that models jet engine design and testing. For his work, NASA recognized him with a Space Act Award . In 2000 he earned his bachelor’s degree in computer science and became a software…

articles.title: Nintendo Is Officially Investing In Game Preservation
articles.content: Nintendo is hiring a digital archivist to help ensure the company's historical records are "preserved for future generations." The 12-month position is tasked with designing and implementing a "structured framework for organizing technical records, engineering documentation, source materials, and institutional knowledge related to legacy systems and platforms." Polygon reports: In the past, Nintendo has drawn criticism from the preservation community. In 2022, the Video Game History Foundation publicly criticized the company for announcing it would be closing the Wii U and 3DS eShops. The foundation released a statement saying that Nintendo's decision was "actively destructive to video game history." The statement also pointed out that Nintendo is part of the Entertainment Software Association, which funds lobbying that prevents a number of preservation efforts. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.author: BeauHD

articles.title: TV deal of the year: LG's stunning C6 OLED TV is half-off today
articles.content: November is the month to buy a new TV. As deals editor, I see great TV deals year-round, but retailers tend to save the best deals for the end of the year. For example, right now you can get the LG 55-inch C6 4K OLED TV for just $999 at Best Buy or Amazon . That's a whopping 50% off and the cheapest price I've seen for this Editor's Choice TV. Want a bigger screen? Best Buy has the LG 65-inch C6 4K OLED TV on sale for $1,399 . That's 48% off and again a new price low for this TV. Here's why I recommend it so much. Quick Links 4K OLED TVs: from $599 @ Best Buy LG 55" C6 4K OLED TV: was $1,299 now $999 @ Best Buy LG 65" C6 4K OLED TV: was $2,699 now $1,399 @ Best Buy LG C6 OLED TV Deals 55" C6 4K OLED TV: was $1999 now $999 The C6 is LG's flagship OLED TV for 2026. In our LG C6 OLED TV review we said the Editor's Choice TV performs brilliantly offering top-tier brightness and colors. We're also fans of its gameplay enhancing features including a new Game Optimizer mode that obliterates input lag and boosts FPS on both consoles and PCs. It's predecessor, the C5, is still a great TV and cheaper, but if you want the latest and greatest — you won't be disappointed with the C6. View Deal 65" C6 4K OLED TV: was $2699 now $1399 Want a bigger size? You can get the 65-inch LG C6 for $1,399. That's 48% off and the cheapest price I've seen for this size. View Deal Whether you're prepping for the release of GTA 6 or looking for the best TV-viewing experience possible, the LG C6 will not disappoint. The C6 doesn't rely on a traditional backlighting, but instead packs millions of self-illuminating pixels. This means that the C6 can render perfect black levels. Additionally, bright objects aren't saddled with the distracting, hazy-looking light bloom you're bound to see on Mini-LED TVs that cost roughly the same as the C6. The C6 also comes with Dolby Vision support. This is one of the most popular HDR formats, and its inclusion ensures that the C6 is able to accurately match a filmmaker's vision when you're watching Dolby Vision-mastered content. When it comes to connectivity, the C6 is again hard to beat. All four of its HDMI 2.1 inputs support 4K gaming at 120Hz (the highest 4K spec for today's consoles), and 4K/165Hz is an option for PC gamers. Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) and AMD FreeSync Premium are along for the ride, too. As a Roku fan, I don't love LG's built-in webOS platform, but that's a minor gripe against an otherwise excellent TV. Will it get cheaper on Black Friday? It's possible, but not likely. This is a premium TV and even if retailers do lower its price again — it won't be a big difference. So now is an excellent time to pick up this TV and have it in your living room well before the turkey even hits the oven.

articles.title: Barracuda’s email security gateways bitten by make-me-root vulns
articles.content: Security company Barracuda warns that attackers are exploiting a pre-authentication authorization bypass bug and a command-injection vulnerability in its popular Email Security Gateway (ESG) products that, when chained, could allow the crims to run commands with root privileges. “We have identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations,” the security vendor said in a late Monday night update to its earlier security advisory. Barracuda declined to answer The Register ’s questions, including one about how many organizations have been hit by attackers. A company spokesperson told us that it “worked directly” with the affected businesses “to quickly address the issue. Barracuda acted promptly to remediate the vulnerabilities, releasing patches for affected products.” The vendor disclosed and fixed the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 , last week. CVE-2026-116606 is a 9.3 CVSS-rated, pre-authentication authorization bypass flaw in ESG. While authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have access to the administrative user interface. As Purplecop Security founder Tausif Ahmed said on Tuesday: “If your Email Security Gateway's admin UI is open to the internet, that's the first thing I'd close today.” CVE-2026-111560 is an 8.6-rated command-injection flaw that affects multiple Barracuda products: its ESG, load balancer (ADC), message archiver (BMA), web application firewall (WAF), WAF control center (WCC), and web security gateway (WSG). “If exploited in combination, these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to bypass authorization controls and obtain root access to the device,” Barracuda warned on November 2. At the time, the vendor did not report any active exploitation of either. We don’t yet know who is responsible for the attacks, or whether the intruders gained root access – but if they did, they could steal data, install backdoors, and take full control of affected systems. These types of edge-device exploits have been used by Chinese-government spies , and in 2023 the FBI blamed PRC-linked attackers for a series of attacks that targeted Barracuda ESGs to deploy custom malware and maintain access to high-value networks . According to Mandiant, 27 percent of identified affected organizations were government entities. So if you haven’t already: patch now. ®

articles.title: Anthropic Seeks Record $88.5B Tied To Public Market Debut
articles.content: Anthropic is seeking to secure up to $88.5 billion in its planned IPO and a concurrent private placement, potentially making it the largest-ever fundraise tied to a public market debut. On Tuesday, the AI giant submitted an updated S-1 filing for its upcoming public offering, unveiling new details including a proposed share price range offering size. The offering could set a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.4 trillion for the San Francisco company. Anthropic’s expected valuation comes in below earlier projections, with many investors reportedly forecasting something closer to $2 trillion. That said, even at $1.4 trillion, Anthropic would still be going public at the second-highest valuation in history, topped only by SpaceX ’s June debut. An IPO and a private placement The offering should also provide Anthropic with plentiful capital to pursue its expensive expansion and infrastructure investment plans. For the IPO portion of its fundraise, Anthropic plans to sell just over 800 million shares 1 at $70 to $78 each. At the high end, that would bring in around $62.5 billion — the largest ever IPO fundraise after SpaceX’s $75 billion offering. Anthropic also expects to pull in another $26 billion from a private placement slated to close immediately following the IPO. Investors in this include AMD , Broadcom , Google , Micron Technology , Microsoft , Nvidia and TSMC . Put together, it’s a record-setting capital haul for a company making its market debut, which Anthropic is expected to do later this month on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. Revenue and recent updates Anthropic also recently updated its financial disclosures, showing results through September of this year. For the first nine months of the year, the company had $33.2 billion in revenue, up from $2.5 billion in the same period a year ago. It’s an astounding growth rate, albeit Anthropic is already known for this. The company claims it has the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history, growing revenue from zero at commercial launch in the first quarter of 2023 to $17 billion for the three months ended Sept. 30, 2026. As of yet, however, it’s not profitable. Anthropic posted an operating loss of $1.3 billion for the first nine months of the year, down from $5.2 billion a year earlier. Its net loss widened to $104 billion, up from $25.1 billion a year ago. Related Crunchbase query: Global IPOs For Venture-Backed Companies In 2026 Illustration: Dom Guzman The total offering is for 825 million shares, of which 23.6 million will be from selling shareholders. ↩

articles.title: Microsoft awards $20K grants to 25 Seattle-area nonprofits amid state budget crunch and tax debate
articles.content: Representatives of the 25 nonprofits receiving Microsoft’s first Community-First Grants pose for a photo Monday with company leaders in Redmond with Seattle Mariners star Cal Raleigh and the team’s mascots. (GeekWire Photo / Todd Bishop) The Lighthouse for the Blind is adding braille displays to its computer lab. Friends of the Issaquah Salmon Hatchery is taking its lessons to low-income schools. And Lake Washington High School’s band boosters are replacing marching capes that date to the MS-DOS era. Those are among 25 King County nonprofits that received $20,000 apiece from Microsoft in grants announced this week. It’s the first round of the company’s Community-First Grants, a $1 million program launched in September . Microsoft said it received 813 applications. “Boy, I think we hit a nerve,” said Jane Broom, Microsoft’s senior director of Community Affairs, during an event Monday recognizing the nonprofits on the company’s Redmond campus, featuring Mariners catcher Cal Raleigh and the team’s mascots. The grants are meant for immediate needs, such as replacing a broken-down van or a failed freezer, Broom explained. Nonprofits that already received or were invited to receive Microsoft corporate grants in 2026 weren’t eligible. Funding and the tax debate: Nonprofits are dealing with rising costs and tighter budgets. As a group, their largest funding source is the state government, which is in the middle of an ongoing debate with members of the business community over taxes and economic competitiveness amid a budget crunch. Microsoft is among the companies asserting that current and proposed taxes are hurting the business climate. It’s also the second-largest funder of the state’s nonprofits, behind only the state itself, said Brad Smith, the company’s president and vice chair. “In my view, a healthy nonprofit community actually has aspects of support from more than one source,” Smith said in an interview after the event, noting that state grants are often at risk when a recession forces budget cuts. Where the money goes: Demand is climbing for many of the grant recipients. At Community Lunch on Capitol Hill , which serves free hot meals, it’s up 40% this year, and the diaper bank at Byrd Barr Place has grown from 720 families in 2021 to 1,600, Microsoft said at the event. Friends of the Issaquah Salmon Hatchery gives more than 700 tours during the salmon season. It will use its grant to bring lessons to classrooms, mainly at Title I schools, which serve large numbers of low-income students and often can’t afford a field trip to the hatchery, said Mark Clemens, the group’s executive director. “If they can’t bring the school to the hatchery, we will go out to the school,” said Clemens, a former Scientific American art director, who was creative director of the Modernist Cuisine cookbook project before taking over the nonprofit in 2023. One bonus for the group, which goes by the clever acronym of FISH, was the appearance of the Mariners’ salmon mascots, which joined the group onstage for a photo op when Clemens and his colleagues accepted its grant. Mark Clemens, center, executive director of Friends of the Issaquah Salmon Hatchery, with FISH treasurer Peter Gowell, left, and board member Jeff Norman, joined by Microsoft’s Jane Broom, far left, and La Shanda Hurst, far right, and the Mariners’ salmon mascots. (GeekWire Photo / Todd Bishop) The Lighthouse for the Blind, a Seattle-based nonprofit that employs blind people in manufacturing, retail and other jobs, will use its grant to upgrade its computer training lab with Windows 11 PCs, braille displays and wireless keyboards, said Antonio Rozier, the nonprofit’s IT director. The goal is to keep employees current on screen readers and other tools so they can work alongside sighted colleagues, Rozier said. The Lighthouse also…
